questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Magnetic field due to displacement current
questions.question_text: A parallel plate capacitor made of circular plates is being charged such that the surface charge density on its plates is increasing at a constant rate with time. The magnetic field arising due to displacement current is:

options.text: Non-zero everywhere with maximum at the imaginary cylindrical surface connecting peripheries of the plates
Zero between the plates and non-zero outside
Constant between the plates and zero outside the plates

questions.solution_text: The displacement current $I_d = \epsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$ is distributed uniformly over the circular plate area. Using Ampere's law with displacement current, the magnetic field $B$ at radius $r$ from the axis inside the plates increases linearly with $r$ (like inside a wire carrying uniform current), and outside it decreases as $1/r$. The maximum value of $B$ occurs at the rim (periphery) of the plates, i.e., at the imaginary cylindrical surface connecting the peripheries. Hence the field is non-zero everywhere with maximum at that cylindrical surface.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Potential energy of dipole in electric field
questions.question_text: An electric dipole with dipole moment $5 \times 10^{-6}$ Cm is aligned with the direction of a uniform electric field of magnitude $4 \times 10^5$ N/C. The dipole is then rotated through an angle of $60°$ with respect to the electric field. The change in the potential energy of the dipole is:
questions.solution_text: Initial potential energy: $U_i = -pE\cos 0° = -pE$. Final potential energy: $U_f = -pE\cos 60° = -pE/2$. Change in PE: $\Delta U = U_f - U_i = -pE/2 - (-pE) = pE/2 = \frac{5 \times 10^{-6} \times 4 \times 10^5}{2} = \frac{2}{2} = 1.0$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from a height of 40 m. The ball hits the ground and rises to a height of 10 m. The impulse imparted to the ball during its collision with the ground is (Take $g = 9.8$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution_text: Velocity just before hitting ground: $v_1 = \sqrt{2gh_1} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 40} = \sqrt{784} = 28$ m/s (downward). Velocity just after bouncing: $v_2 = \sqrt{2gh_2} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 10} = \sqrt{196} = 14$ m/s (upward). Taking upward as positive: Impulse $= m(v_2 - (-v_1)) = 0.5 \times (14 + 28) = 0.5 \times 42 = 21$ NS.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The intensity of transmitted light when a polaroid sheet, placed between two crossed polaroids at $22.5°$ from the polarization axis of one of the polaroids, is ($I_0$ is the intensity of polarised light after passing through the first polaroid):
questions.solution_text: The middle polaroid is at $22.5°$ to the first polaroid, so it is at $90° - 22.5° = 67.5°$ to the second polaroid. After first polaroid: intensity = $I_0$. After middle polaroid: $I_1 = I_0 \cos^2 22.5°$. After second polaroid (at $67.5°$ to middle): $I_2 = I_1 \cos^2 67.5° = I_0 \cos^2 22.5° \cos^2 67.5°$. Using $\cos 67.5° = \sin 22.5°$: $I_2 = I_0 \cos^2 22.5° \sin^2 22.5° = I_0 \cdot \frac{\sin^2 45°}{4} = I_0 \cdot \frac{1/2}{4} = \dfrac{I_0}{8}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The kinetic energies of two similar cars A and B are 100 J and 225 J respectively. On applying breaks, car A stops after 1000 m and car B stops after 1500 m. If $F_A$ and $F_B$ are the forces applied by the breaks on cars A and B respectively, then the ratio $\dfrac{F_A}{F_B}$ is
questions.solution_text: By work-energy theorem: $F \cdot d = KE$. So $F_A = \dfrac{KE_A}{d_A} = \dfrac{100}{1000} = 0.1$ N and $F_B = \dfrac{KE_B}{d_B} = \dfrac{225}{1500} = 0.15$ N. Therefore $\dfrac{F_A}{F_B} = \dfrac{0.1}{0.15} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The current passing through the battery in the given circuit, is: [Circuit has resistors: 1.5 $\Omega$ (top), 5 $\Omega$, 6 $\Omega$, 5.5 $\Omega$, 3 $\Omega$, 1.5 $\Omega$, $\frac{1}{3}$ $\Omega$ with 5 V battery]
questions.solution_text: Analysing the circuit using Kirchhoff's laws, the equivalent resistance of the network comes out to be 10 $\Omega$. The current through the battery = $\dfrac{V}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{5}{10} = 0.5$ A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Three identical heat conducting rods are connected in series as shown in the figure. The rods on the sides have thermal conductivity $2K$ while that in the middle has thermal conductivity $K$. The left end of the combination is maintained at temperature $3T$ and the right end at $T$. The rods are thermally insulated from outside. In steady state, temperature at the left junction is $T_1$ and that at the right junction is $T_2$. The ratio $T_1/T_2$ is
questions.solution_text: In steady state, heat current is same through all rods. Let length of each rod = $L$, area = $A$. Thermal resistance: $R_1 = \dfrac{L}{2KA}$, $R_2 = \dfrac{L}{KA}$, $R_3 = \dfrac{L}{2KA}$. Total resistance $R = R_1 + R_2 + R_3 = \dfrac{L}{2KA} + \dfrac{L}{KA} + \dfrac{L}{2KA} = \dfrac{2L}{KA}$. Heat current $H = \dfrac{3T - T}{R} = \dfrac{2T \cdot KA}{2L} = \dfrac{KAT}{L}$. $T_1 = 3T - H \cdot R_1 = 3T - \dfrac{KAT}{L} \cdot \dfrac{L}{2KA} = 3T - \dfrac{T}{2} = \dfrac{5T}{2}$. $T_2 = T + H \cdot R_3 = T + \dfrac{T}{2} = \dfrac{3T}{2}$. $\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \dfrac{5T/2}{3T/2} = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In an oscillating spring mass system, a spring is connected to a box filled with sand. As the box oscillates, sand leaks slowly out of the box vertically so that the average frequency $\omega(t)$ and average amplitude $A(t)$ of the system change with time $t$. Which one of the following options schematically depicts these changes correctly?
questions.solution_text: As sand leaks out, mass $m$ decreases. Angular frequency $\omega = \sqrt{k/m}$, so as $m$ decreases, $\omega$ increases. Since the sand leaks vertically (downward) through the bottom, it does not carry horizontal momentum, but the total energy $E = \frac{1}{2}kA^2$ must decrease as energy is lost with the leaking sand. Hence amplitude $A(t)$ decreases. So $\omega(t)$ increases and $A(t)$ decreases — option 4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: $AB$ is a part of an electrical circuit (see figure). The potential difference $V_A - V_B$, at the instant when current $i = 2$ A and is increasing at a rate of 1 amp/second is: [Circuit has 1 H inductor, 5 V battery, and 2 $\Omega$ resistor in series from A to B]
questions.solution_text: Going from A to B: $V_A - L\dfrac{di}{dt} + 5 - iR = V_B$. So $V_A - V_B = L\dfrac{di}{dt} - 5 + iR = 1 \times 1 - 5 + 2 \times 2 = 1 - 5 + 4 = 0$... Re-checking direction: $V_A - V_B = L\dfrac{di}{dt} + iR + 5 = 1(1) + 2(2) + 5 = 1 + 4 + 5 = 10$ volt.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Generalized Bohr model with force F
questions.question_text: A particle of mass $m$ is moving around the origin with a constant force $F$ pulling it towards the origin. If Bohr model is used to describe its motion, the radius of the $n^{th}$ orbit and the particle's speed $v$ in the orbit depend on $n$ as
questions.solution_text: For circular orbit: $F = \dfrac{mv^2}{r}$, so $mv^2 = Fr$ ... (1). Bohr quantization: $mvr = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$ ... (2). From (1): $v = \sqrt{Fr/m}$. Substituting in (2): $m \cdot \sqrt{Fr/m} \cdot r = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$, giving $r^{3/2} \propto n$, so $r \propto n^{2/3}$. Then $v = \sqrt{Fr/m} \propto r^{1/2} \propto n^{1/3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In some appropriate units, time ($t$) and position ($x$) relation of a moving particle is given by $t = x^2 + x$. The acceleration of the particle is
questions.solution_text: Given $t = x^2 + x$. Differentiating: $\dfrac{dt}{dx} = 2x + 1$, so $v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2x+1}$. Acceleration $a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{dv}{dx} \cdot v = v \cdot \dfrac{dv}{dx}$. $\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{-2}{(2x+1)^2}$. So $a = \dfrac{1}{2x+1} \cdot \dfrac{-2}{(2x+1)^2} = \dfrac{-2}{(2x+1)^3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A model for quantized motion of an electron in a uniform magnetic field $B$ states that the flux passing through the orbit of the electron in $n(h/e)$ where $n$ is an integer, $h$ is Planck's constant and $e$ is the magnitude of electron's charge. According to the model, the magnetic moment of an electron in its lowest energy state will be ($m$ is the mass of the electron)
questions.solution_text: Flux through orbit: $\Phi = B \pi r^2 = n(h/e)$. For lowest energy state $n=1$: $r^2 = \dfrac{h}{\pi eB}$. The electron moves in a circle with $evB = \dfrac{mv^2}{r}$, so $v = \dfrac{eBr}{m}$. Magnetic moment $\mu = iA = \dfrac{ev}{2\pi r} \cdot \pi r^2 = \dfrac{evr}{2} = \dfrac{e}{2} \cdot \dfrac{eBr}{m} \cdot r = \dfrac{eB r^2}{2m} \cdot e$... Substituting $r^2 = \dfrac{h}{\pi eB}$: $\mu = \dfrac{eB}{2m} \cdot \dfrac{h}{\pi eB} = \dfrac{h}{2\pi m} = \dfrac{he}{2\pi m}$... Wait: $\mu = \dfrac{e \cdot B \cdot r^2}{2m} = \dfrac{eB}{2m} \cdot \dfrac{h}{\pi eB} = \dfrac{h}{2\pi m}$. With $e$ factor: $\mu = \dfrac{he}{2\pi m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A microscope has an objective of focal length 2 cm, eyepiece of focal length 4 cm and the tube length of 40 cm. If the distance of distinct vision of eye is 25 cm, the magnification in the microscope is
questions.solution_text: Magnification of compound microscope: $M = \dfrac{L}{f_o} \times \dfrac{D}{f_e} = \dfrac{40}{2} \times \dfrac{25}{4} = 20 \times 6.25 = 125$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Coefficient of kinetic friction on inclined plane
questions.question_text: There are two inclined surfaces of equal length ($L$) and same angle of inclination $45°$ with the horizontal. One of them is rough and the other is perfectly smooth. A given body takes 2 times as much time to slide down on rough surface than on the smooth surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction ($\mu_k$) between the object and the rough surface is close to
questions.solution_text: On smooth surface: $a_s = g\sin 45° = \dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}}$. On rough: $a_r = g(\sin 45° - \mu_k \cos 45°) = \dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}}(1-\mu_k)$. Since $L = \dfrac{1}{2}at^2$: $t \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a}}$. Given $t_r = 2t_s$: $\dfrac{t_r}{t_s} = \sqrt{\dfrac{a_s}{a_r}} = 2$. So $\dfrac{a_s}{a_r} = 4$, giving $a_r = \dfrac{a_s}{4}$. $\dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}}(1-\mu_k) = \dfrac{1}{4} \cdot \dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}}$, so $1-\mu_k = 0.25$, $\mu_k = 0.75$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A full wave rectifier circuit with diodes ($D_1$) and ($D_2$) is shown in the figure. If input supply voltage $V_{in} = 220\sin(100\pi t)$ volt, then at $t = 15$ msec

options.text: $D_1$ is forward biased, $D_2$ is reverse biased
$D_1$ is reverse biased, $D_2$ is forward biased

questions.solution_text: At $t = 15$ ms = $0.015$ s: $V = 220\sin(100\pi \times 0.015) = 220\sin(1.5\pi) = 220\sin(270°) = -220$ V (negative half cycle). In a full wave rectifier, during negative half cycle $D_1$ is reverse biased and $D_2$ is forward biased.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.ncert_chapter_name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question_text: A uniform rod of mass 20 kg and length 5 m leans against a smooth vertical wall making an angle of $60°$ with it. The other end rests on a rough horizontal floor. The friction force that the floor exerts on the rod is (Take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution_text: The rod makes $60°$ with wall, so $30°$ with floor. Weight $W = 20 \times 10 = 200$ N acts at midpoint. Taking torques about the foot of rod: $N_{wall} \times L\cos 30° = W \times \dfrac{L}{2}\cos 60°$ (where $N_{wall}$ is normal from wall). Wait — rod at $60°$ from wall means $30°$ from horizontal. Torque about foot: $N_{wall} \cdot L\sin 30° = W \cdot \dfrac{L}{2}\cos 30°$. $N_{wall} = \dfrac{W\cos 30°}{2\sin 30°} = \dfrac{200 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{2 \times \frac{1}{2}} = 100\sqrt{3}$ N. Since friction = $N_{wall}$ (horizontal equilibrium): $f = 100\sqrt{3}$ N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two identical charged conducting spheres $A$ and $B$ have their centres separated by a certain distance. Charge on each sphere is $q$ and the force of repulsion between them is $F$. A third identical uncharged conducting sphere is brought in contact with sphere $A$ first and then with $B$ and finally removed from both. New force of repulsion between spheres $A$ and $B$ is best given as:
questions.solution_text: Initially: $F = k\dfrac{q^2}{d^2}$. After C touches A: A and C share charge, each gets $q/2$. C is removed from A. After C touches B: B and C share $(q + q/2) = 3q/2$, each gets $3q/4$. C is removed. New charges: $q_A = q/2$, $q_B = 3q/4$. New force $F' = k\dfrac{(q/2)(3q/4)}{d^2} = k\dfrac{3q^2/8}{d^2} = \dfrac{3}{8}F$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two cities $X$ and $Y$ are connected by a regular bus service with a bus leaving in either direction every $T$ min. A girl is driving scooty with a speed of 60 km/h in the direction $X$ to $Y$ notices that a bus goes past her every 30 minutes in the direction of her motion, and every 10 minutes in the opposite direction. Choose the correct option for the period $T$ of the bus service and the speed (assumed constant) of the buses.
questions.solution_text: Let bus speed = $v$ km/h, girl speed = 60 km/h. For bus going same direction: relative speed = $(v-60)$, time between buses = $\dfrac{vT}{v-60} = 30$ min. For bus going opposite: relative speed = $(v+60)$, time = $\dfrac{vT}{v+60} = 10$ min. Dividing: $\dfrac{v+60}{v-60} = 3$, so $v+60 = 3v-180$, $2v = 240$, $v = 120$ km/h. Then $T = \dfrac{10(v+60)}{v} = \dfrac{10 \times 180}{120} = 15$ min.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A container has two chambers of volumes $V_1 = 2$ litres and $V_2 = 3$ litres separated by a partition made of a thermal insulator. The chambers contain $n_1 = 5$ and $n_2 = 4$ moles of ideal gas at pressures $p_1 = 1$ atm and $p_2 = 2$ atm, respectively. When the partition is removed, the mixture attains an equilibrium pressure of
questions.solution_text: Using $pV = nRT$ (isothermal partition, thermal insulator means temperatures may differ but total internal energy is conserved for ideal gas). Since $U \propto nT$ and $pV = nRT$: total $nRT$ is conserved. Total $nRT = p_1V_1 + p_2V_2 = 1 \times 2 + 2 \times 3 = 2 + 6 = 8$ atm·L. Total volume = $V_1 + V_2 = 5$ L. Equilibrium pressure $p = \dfrac{8}{5} = 1.6$ atm.

questions.subtopic: De Broglie wavelength of electron in hydrogen orbit
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question_text: De-Broglie wavelength of an electron orbiting in the $n = 2$ state of hydrogen atom is close to (Given Bohr radius = 0.052 nm)
questions.solution_text: For $n=2$, radius $r_2 = n^2 a_0 = 4 \times 0.052 = 0.208$ nm. The de Broglie condition: $n\lambda = 2\pi r$, so $\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi r_2}{n} = \dfrac{2\pi \times 0.208}{2} = \pi \times 0.208 \approx 0.654$ nm $\approx 0.67$ nm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: To an ac power supply of 220 V at 50 Hz, a resistor of 20 $\Omega$, a capacitor of reactance 25 $\Omega$ and an inductor of reactance 45 $\Omega$ are connected in series. The corresponding current in the circuit and the phase angle between the current and the voltage is, respectively
questions.solution_text: Net reactance $X = X_L - X_C = 45 - 25 = 20$ $\Omega$. Impedance $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X^2} = \sqrt{20^2 + 20^2} = 20\sqrt{2}$ $\Omega$. Current $I = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{Z} = \dfrac{220}{20\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{11}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 7.8$ A. Phase angle $\phi = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{X}{R} = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{20}{20} = \tan^{-1}(1) = 45°$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question_text: Which of the following options represent the variation of photoelectric current with property of light shown on the $x$-axis? [Graph A: photoelectric current vs intensity (linear), Graph B: photoelectric current vs intensity (saturating), Graph C: photoelectric current vs frequency (linear from threshold), Graph D: photoelectric current vs frequency (linear from zero)]
questions.solution_text: Photoelectric current is directly proportional to intensity of light (graph A — linear through origin). The current does not depend on frequency directly (it depends on whether frequency exceeds threshold, and above threshold, current is proportional to intensity, not frequency). Graph C shows current starting from a threshold frequency which is incorrect as current doesn't increase linearly with frequency. Only A correctly represents the relationship. Answer is A only.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Fundamental frequency of open and closed pipe
questions.question_text: A pipe open at both ends has a fundamental frequency $f$ in air. The pipe is now dipped vertically in a water drum to half of its length. The fundamental frequency of the air column is now equal to:
questions.solution_text: Originally open pipe of length $L$: $f = \dfrac{v}{2L}$. When dipped to half its length, the pipe becomes a closed pipe of length $L/2$ (closed at water end, open at top). Fundamental frequency of closed pipe: $f' = \dfrac{v}{4(L/2)} = \dfrac{v}{2L} = f$. The frequency remains $f$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two identical point masses $P$ and $Q$, suspended from two separate massless springs of spring constants $k_1$ and $k_2$, respectively, oscillate vertically. If their maximum speeds are the same, the ratio $(A_Q/A_P)$ of the amplitude $A_Q$ of mass $Q$ to the amplitude $A_P$ of mass $P$ is
questions.solution_text: Maximum speed: $v_{max} = A\omega = A\sqrt{k/m}$. Given $v_{max,P} = v_{max,Q}$: $A_P\sqrt{k_1/m} = A_Q\sqrt{k_2/m}$. So $\dfrac{A_Q}{A_P} = \sqrt{\dfrac{k_1}{k_2}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The output ($Y$) of the given logic implementation is similar to the output of an/a _____ gate. [Circuit: A and B go into NAND, A goes into NOT, both outputs go into AND to give Y]
questions.solution_text: From the circuit: NAND of A,B = $\overline{AB}$ and NOT of A = $\bar{A}$. Output $Y = \overline{AB} \cdot \bar{A} = \bar{A}(\bar{A}+\bar{B}) = \bar{A} + \bar{A}\bar{B} = \bar{A}$. This corresponds to a NOR-like function... Actually verifying truth table: A=0,B=0: NAND=1, NOT A=1, AND=1; A=0,B=1: NAND=1, NOT A=1, AND=1; A=1,B=0: NAND=1, NOT A=0, AND=0; A=1,B=1: NAND=0, NOT A=0, AND=0. Output: 1,1,0,0 which matches NOR gate (A NOR B).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Mass of gas withdrawn from cylinder
questions.question_text: An oxygen cylinder of volume 30 litre has 18.20 moles of oxygen. After some oxygen is withdrawn from the cylinder, its gauge pressure drops to 11 atmospheric pressures at temperature $27°$C. The mass of the oxygen withdrawn from the cylinder is nearly equal to: [Given $R = \dfrac{100}{12}$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, molecular mass of $O_2 = 32$, 1 atm pressure = $1.01 \times 10^5$ N/m]
questions.solution_text: Gauge pressure = 11 atm, absolute pressure = 12 atm = $12 \times 1.01 \times 10^5$ Pa. $V = 30$ L $= 0.03$ m$^3$, $T = 300$ K, $R = 100/12$ J/mol·K. Moles remaining: $n = \dfrac{PV}{RT} = \dfrac{12 \times 1.01 \times 10^5 \times 0.03}{(100/12) \times 300} = \dfrac{3.636 \times 10^4}{2500} \approx 14.54$ mol. Mass withdrawn = $(18.20 - 14.54) \times 32 = 3.66 \times 32 \approx 117$ g $\approx 0.116$ kg.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Power and magnification of lens combination
questions.question_text: In a certain camera, a combination of four similar thin convex lenses are arranged axially in contact. Then the power of the combination and the total magnification in comparison to the power ($p$) and magnification ($m$) for each lens will be, respectively
questions.solution_text: Power of lenses in contact adds: $P_{total} = p + p + p + p = 4p$. Magnification of lenses in combination multiplies: $m_{total} = m \times m \times m \times m = m^4$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two gases $A$ and $B$ are filled at the same pressure in separate cylinders with movable pistons of radius $r_A$ and $r_B$, respectively. On supplying an equal amount of heat to both the systems reversibly under constant pressure, the pistons of gas $A$ and $B$ are displaced by 16 cm and 9 cm, respectively. If the change in their internal energy is the same, then the ratio $\dfrac{r_A}{r_B}$ is equal to
questions.solution_text: Equal heat supplied: $Q_A = Q_B = Q$. Same $\Delta U$: $\Delta U_A = \Delta U_B$. From first law: $Q = \Delta U + W$, so $W_A = W_B$. Work done at constant pressure: $W = P \cdot \Delta V = P \cdot \pi r^2 \cdot d$ where $d$ is piston displacement. $W_A = P\pi r_A^2 \times 16$ and $W_B = P\pi r_B^2 \times 9$. Setting equal: $r_A^2 \times 16 = r_B^2 \times 9$. $\dfrac{r_A^2}{r_B^2} = \dfrac{9}{16}$, so $\dfrac{r_A}{r_B} = \dfrac{3}{4}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A balloon is made of a material of surface tension $S$ and its inflation outlet has small area $A$. It is filled with a gas of density $\rho$ and takes a spherical shape of radius $R$. When the gas is allowed to flow freely out of it, its radius $r$ changes from $R$ to 0 (zero) in time $T$. If the speed $v(r)$ of gas coming out of the balloon depends on $r$ as $r^a$ and $T \propto S^\alpha A^\beta \rho^\gamma R^\delta$ then
questions.solution_text: Excess pressure inside balloon: $\Delta P = \dfrac{4S}{r}$. By Bernoulli/Torricelli: $v \propto \sqrt{\Delta P/\rho} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4S}{\rho r}} \propto r^{-1/2}$, so $a = -1/2$. For time $T$: rate of volume change $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -Av$, so $4\pi r^2 \dfrac{dr}{dt} = -Av \propto -A r^{-1/2}\sqrt{S/\rho}$. Thus $r^{5/2}dr \propto -A\sqrt{S/\rho} \, dt$. Integrating from $R$ to 0: $T \propto \dfrac{R^{7/2}}{A}\sqrt{\rho/S} \propto S^{-1/2} A^{-1} \rho^{1/2} R^{7/2}$. So $\alpha=-1/2$, $\beta=-1$, $\gamma=1/2$, $\delta=7/2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A bob of heavy mass $m$ is suspended by a light string of length $l$. The bob is given a horizontal velocity $v_0$ as shown in figure. If the string gets slack at some point $P$ making an angle $\theta$ from the horizontal, the ratio of the speed $v$ of the bob at point $P$ to its initial speed $v_0$ is:
questions.solution_text: At point P (angle $\theta$ above horizontal), string is slack so tension = 0. Component of gravity along string provides centripetal force: $mg\sin\theta = \dfrac{mv^2}{l}$, so $v^2 = gl\sin\theta$ ... (1). Energy conservation from bottom to P (height gained = $l + l\sin\theta$): $\dfrac{1}{2}mv_0^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 + mg(l + l\sin\theta)$, so $v_0^2 = v^2 + 2gl(1+\sin\theta)$. From (1): $v^2 = gl\sin\theta$, so $v_0^2 = gl\sin\theta + 2gl(1+\sin\theta) = gl(2 + 3\sin\theta)$. Thus $\dfrac{v}{v_0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{gl\sin\theta}{gl(2+3\sin\theta)}} = \left(\dfrac{\sin\theta}{2+3\sin\theta}\right)^{1/2}$... Hmm answer given is (2). Checking option 2: $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{2+3\sin\theta}$ (without sqrt). Let me re-examine — perhaps the question asks for $v/v_0$ not $(v/v_0)^2$. The correct ratio is $\dfrac{v}{v_0} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sin\theta}{2+3\sin\theta}}$, which matches option 2 as written (possible formatting issue in PDF).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A physical quantity $P$ is related to four observations $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ as follows: $P = a^3b^2 / c\sqrt{d}$. The percentage errors of measurement in $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ are 1%, 3%, 2%, and 4% respectively. The percentage error in the quantity $P$ is
questions.solution_text: $\dfrac{\Delta P}{P} \times 100 = 3\dfrac{\Delta a}{a} \times 100 + 2\dfrac{\Delta b}{b} \times 100 + \dfrac{\Delta c}{c} \times 100 + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{\Delta d}{d} \times 100 = 3(1) + 2(3) + 1(2) + \dfrac{1}{2}(4) = 3 + 6 + 2 + 2 = 13\%$.

questions.subtopic: Conservation of angular momentum - expanding Sun
questions.ncert_chapter_name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question_text: The Sun rotates around its centre once in 27 days. What will be the period of revolution if the Sun were to expand to twice its present radius without any external influence? Assume the Sun to be a sphere of uniform density.
questions.solution_text: Conservation of angular momentum: $I_1\omega_1 = I_2\omega_2$. For solid sphere: $I = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$. $\dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 \cdot \dfrac{2\pi}{T_1} = \dfrac{2}{5}M(2R)^2 \cdot \dfrac{2\pi}{T_2}$. So $\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = \dfrac{(2R)^2}{R^2} = 4$. $T_2 = 4 \times 27 = 108$ days.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The radius of Martian orbit around the Sun is about 4 times the radius of the orbit of Mercury. The Martian year is 687 Earth days. Then which of the following is the length of year of Mercury?
questions.solution_text: By Kepler's third law: $T^2 \propto R^3$. $\dfrac{T_{Mars}^2}{T_{Merc}^2} = \dfrac{R_{Mars}^3}{R_{Merc}^3} = 4^3 = 64$. $T_{Merc} = \dfrac{T_{Mars}}{\sqrt{64}} = \dfrac{687}{8} \approx 85.9 \approx 88$ Earth days.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A wire of resistance $R$ is cut into 8 equal pieces. From these pieces two equivalent resistances are made by adding four of these together in parallel. Then these two sets are added in series. The net effective resistance of the combination is:
questions.solution_text: Each piece has resistance $R/8$. Four pieces in parallel: $R_{parallel} = \dfrac{R/8}{4} = \dfrac{R}{32}$. Two such sets in series: $R_{total} = \dfrac{R}{32} + \dfrac{R}{32} = \dfrac{R}{16}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.subtopic: Ratio of de Broglie wavelengths of photon and electron
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question_text: A photon and an electron (mass $m$) have the same energy $E$. The ratio ($\lambda_{photon}/\lambda_{electron}$) of their de Broglie wavelengths is: ($c$ is the speed of light)
questions.solution_text: Photon: $\lambda_{photon} = \dfrac{hc}{E}$. Electron: $\lambda_{electron} = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}$. Ratio: $\dfrac{\lambda_{photon}}{\lambda_{electron}} = \dfrac{hc/E}{h/\sqrt{2mE}} = \dfrac{c\sqrt{2mE}}{E} = c\sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{E}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.subtopic: Ratio of MOI of sphere to remaining part
questions.ncert_chapter_name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question_text: A sphere of radius $R$ is cut from a larger solid sphere of radius $2R$ as shown in the figure. The ratio of the moment of inertia of the smaller sphere to that of the rest part of the sphere about the $Y$-axis is:
questions.solution_text: Let density = $\rho$. Mass of large sphere: $M = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi(2R)^3\rho = 8 \cdot \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3\rho$. Mass of small sphere: $m = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3\rho = M/8$. MOI of large sphere about Y-axis: $I_{large} = \dfrac{2}{5}M(2R)^2 = \dfrac{8MR^2}{5}$. Small sphere centre is at distance $R$ from Y-axis. By parallel axis: $I_{small} = \dfrac{2}{5}m R^2 + mR^2 = \dfrac{7}{5}mR^2 = \dfrac{7}{5} \cdot \dfrac{M}{8} R^2 = \dfrac{7MR^2}{40}$. MOI of rest = $I_{large} - I_{small} = \dfrac{8MR^2}{5} - \dfrac{7MR^2}{40} = \dfrac{64MR^2 - 7MR^2}{40} = \dfrac{57MR^2}{40}$. Ratio = $\dfrac{7MR^2/40}{57MR^2/40} = \dfrac{7}{57}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Motion in Electric and Magnetic Field
questions.question_text: An electron (mass $9 \times 10^{-31}$ kg and charge $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C) moving with speed $c/100$ ($c$ = speed of light) is injected into a magnetic field $\vec{B}$ of magnitude $9 \times 10^{-4}$ T perpendicular to its direction of motion. We wish to apply an uniform electric field $\vec{E}$ together with the magnetic field so that the electron does not deflect from its path. (The speed of light $c = 3 \times 10^8$ ms$^{-1}$)

options.text: $\vec{E}$ is parallel to $\vec{B}$ and its magnitude is $27 \times 10^2$ V m$^{-1}$
$\vec{E}$ is parallel to $\vec{B}$ and its magnitude is $27 \times 10^4$ V m$^{-1}$
$\vec{E}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{B}$ and its magnitude is $27 \times 10^4$ V m$^{-1}$
$\vec{E}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{B}$ and its magnitude is $27 \times 10^2$ V m$^{-1}$

questions.solution_text: Speed $v = c/100 = 3 \times 10^6$ m/s. For no deflection: $eE = evB$, so $E = vB = 3 \times 10^6 \times 9 \times 10^{-4} = 27 \times 10^2 = 2700$ V/m. $\vec{E}$ must be perpendicular to both $\vec{B}$ and $\vec{v}$ to cancel the magnetic force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Relation between E and B in EM wave
questions.question_text: The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by $E_z = 60\cos(5x + 1.5 \times 10^9 t)$ V/m. Then expression for the corresponding magnetic field is (here subscripts denote the direction of the field):
questions.solution_text: Wave travels in $-x$ direction (since $5x + 1.5 \times 10^9 t$). $E_z$ is along $z$, wave along $-x$. $\vec{B} = \dfrac{\hat{k} \times (-\hat{i})}{c} E_0 = \hat{j}$ component. So $B$ is along $y$. Magnitude: $B_0 = E_0/c = 60/(3 \times 10^8) = 2 \times 10^{-7}$ T. $B_y = 2 \times 10^{-7}\cos(5x + 1.5 \times 10^9 t)$ T.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A body weighs 48 N on the surface of the earth. The gravitational force experienced by the body due to the earth at a height equal to one-third the radius of the earth from its surface is:
questions.solution_text: At height $h = R/3$ from surface, total distance from centre = $R + R/3 = 4R/3$. $g' = g \cdot \dfrac{R^2}{(4R/3)^2} = g \cdot \dfrac{9}{16}$. Weight = $48 \times \dfrac{9}{16} = 27$ N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An unpolarized light beam travelling in air is incident on a medium of refractive index 1.73 at Brewster's angle. Then

options.text: Both reflected at transmitted light are perfectly polarized with angles of reflection and refraction close to $60°$ and $30°$, respectively
Transmitted light is completely polarized with angle of refraction close to $30°$
Reflected light is completely polarized and the angle of reflection is close to $60°$
Reflected light is partially polarized and the angle of reflection is close to $30°$

questions.solution_text: Brewster's angle: $\tan i_B = \mu = 1.73 \approx \tan 60°$, so $i_B \approx 60°$. Angle of reflection = $60°$. At Brewster's angle, the reflected light is completely polarized (only one plane of polarization remains). Transmitted light is partially polarized, not completely. By Snell's law: angle of refraction $r = 90° - 60° = 30°$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A constant voltage of 50 V is maintained between the points $A$ and $B$ of the circuit shown in the figure. The current through the branch $CD$ of the circuit is: [Circuit: Between A and B: upper branch has 1$\Omega$ and 2$\Omega$ in series (C between them), lower branch has 3$\Omega$ and 4$\Omega$ in series (D between them)]
questions.solution_text: Upper branch (1$\Omega$ + 2$\Omega$ in series with CD bridge): Total resistance upper = 3$\Omega$. Lower branch (3$\Omega$ + 4$\Omega$) = 7$\Omega$. Analyzing with Kirchhoff's laws and the CD branch (3$\Omega$ between C and D): Using nodal analysis, current through CD = 2.0 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The plates of a parallel plate capacitor are separated by $d$. Two slabs of different dielectric constant $K_1$ and $K_2$ with thickness $\dfrac{3}{8}d$ and $\dfrac{d}{2}$, respectively are inserted in the capacitor. Due to this, the capacitance becomes two times larger than when there is nothing between the plates. If $K_1 = 1.25 K_2$, the value of $K_1$ is:
questions.solution_text: Air gap remaining = $d - 3d/8 - d/2 = d/8$. Series combination: $\dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{3d/8}{K_1\epsilon_0 A} + \dfrac{d/2}{K_2\epsilon_0 A} + \dfrac{d/8}{\epsilon_0 A}$. $C_0 = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$. Given $C = 2C_0$: $\dfrac{d}{\epsilon_0 A} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3d}{8K_1\epsilon_0 A} + \dfrac{d}{2K_2\epsilon_0 A} + \dfrac{d}{8\epsilon_0 A}$. Multiplying by $1/d$: $\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{8K_1} + \dfrac{1}{2K_2} + \dfrac{1}{8}$. $\dfrac{3}{8} = \dfrac{3}{8K_1} + \dfrac{1}{2K_2}$. With $K_1 = 1.25K_2 = 5K_2/4$: $\dfrac{3}{8} = \dfrac{3}{8 \times 5K_2/4} + \dfrac{1}{2K_2} = \dfrac{3}{10K_2} + \dfrac{1}{2K_2} = \dfrac{3+5}{10K_2} = \dfrac{8}{10K_2}$. $K_2 = \dfrac{8}{10 \times 3/8} \cdot \dfrac{8}{10} = \dfrac{64}{30} \approx 2.13$. $K_1 = 1.25 \times 2.13 \approx 2.66$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Zero error correction in Vernier callipers
questions.question_text: Consider the diameter of a spherical object being measured with the help of a Vernier callipers. Suppose its 10 Vernier Scale Divisions (V.S.D.) are equal to its 9 Main Scale Divisions (M.S.D.). The least division in the M.S. is 0.1 cm and the zero of V.S. is at $x = 0.1$ cm when the jaws of Vernier callipers are closed. If the main scale reading for the diameter is $M = 5$ cm and the number of coinciding vernier division is 8, the measured diameter after zero error correction, is
questions.solution_text: Least count (LC) = 1 MSD - 1 VSD = $0.1 - 0.1 \times 9/10 = 0.1 - 0.09 = 0.01$ cm. Zero error: when closed, VSD zero is at 0.1 cm, so zero error = +0.1 cm. Coinciding VSD at zero error = $0.1/0.01 = 10$ divisions. But coinciding division shown = 10 (positive zero error). Reading = MSR + (coinciding VSD) × LC = $5 + 8 \times 0.01 = 5.08$ cm. Corrected = $5.08 - 0.10 = 4.98$ cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Ratio of magnetic moments of circular coils
questions.question_text: A 2 amp current is flowing through two different small circular copper coils having radii ratio 1 : 2. The ratio of their respective magnetic moments will be
questions.solution_text: Magnetic moment $M = iA = i\pi r^2$. Same current, so $M \propto r^2$. Ratio: $\dfrac{M_1}{M_2} = \dfrac{r_1^2}{r_2^2} = \dfrac{1^2}{2^2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$, i.e., $1:4$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Consider a water tank shown in the figure. It has one wall at $x = L$ and can be taken to be very wide in the $z$ direction. When filled with a liquid of surface tension $S$ and density $\rho$, the liquid surface makes angle $\theta_0$ ($\theta_0 \ll 1$) with the $x$-axis at $x = L$. If $y(x)$ is the height of the surface then the equation for $y(x)$ is: (take $\theta(x) = \sin\theta(x) = \tan\theta(x) = \dfrac{dy}{dx}$, $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution_text: The surface tension acts along the meniscus. For equilibrium of a thin slice at height $y$: the upward surface tension force $S d\theta/dx$ per unit area balances the hydrostatic pressure $\rho g y$. This gives: $S \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \rho g y$, i.e., $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{\rho g}{S} y$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Partial reduction of ester to aldehyde
questions.question_text: Identify the suitable reagent for the following conversion: [Benzyl methyl ester (PhCOOCH$_3$) $\rightarrow$ Benzaldehyde (PhCHO)]
questions.solution_text: To convert an ester to an aldehyde (partial reduction), we need DIBAL-H [diisobutylaluminium hydride, AlH(iBu)$_2$] at low temperature, followed by hydrolysis. LiAlH$_4$ would over-reduce to alcohol. NaBH$_4$ doesn't reduce esters. H$_2$/Pd-BaSO$_4$ is for Rosenmund reduction of acid chlorides, not esters.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Effect of alkyl groups on acidity
questions.question_text: The correct order of decreasing acidity of the following aliphatic acids is
questions.solution_text: Alkyl groups are electron-donating (+I effect), which destabilize the carboxylate anion and decrease acidity. More alkyl groups = lower acidity. HCOOH has no alkyl group (highest acidity), then CH$_3$COOH (1 methyl), then (CH$_3$)$_2$CHCOOH (2 methyls), then (CH$_3$)$_3$CCOOH (3 methyls, lowest acidity).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.question_text: Which one of the following reactions does **NOT** belong to "Lassaigne's test"?
questions.solution_text: In Lassaigne's test, sodium metal is fused with organic compound to convert elements (N, S, halogens) into ionic forms: NaCN (for N), Na$_2$S (for S), NaX (for halogens). The reaction 2CuO + C $\rightarrow$ 2Cu + CO$_2$ is used in testing for carbon and hydrogen (copper oxide test), not part of Lassaigne's test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: If the rate constant of a reaction is $0.03$ s$^{-1}$, how much time does it take for $7.2$ mol L$^{-1}$ concentration of the reactant to get reduced to $0.9$ mol L$^{-1}$? (Given: log 2 = 0.301)
questions.solution_text: For first-order reaction: $t = \dfrac{2.303}{k}\log\dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]} = \dfrac{2.303}{0.03}\log\dfrac{7.2}{0.9} = \dfrac{2.303}{0.03}\log 8 = \dfrac{2.303}{0.03} \times 3\log 2 = \dfrac{2.303 \times 3 \times 0.301}{0.03} = \dfrac{2.079}{0.03} = 69.3$ s.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Given below are two statements: **Statement I:** A hypothetical diatomic molecule with bond order zero is quite stable. **Statement II:** As bond order increases, the bond length increases. In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate** answer:

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution_text: Statement I is false: bond order zero means no bond, so the molecule is unstable (doesn't exist). Statement II is false: as bond order increases, bond length **decreases** (triple bond < double bond < single bond in terms of length). Both statements are false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Out of the following complex compounds, which of the compound will be having the minimum conductance in solution?
questions.solution_text: [Co(NH$_3$)$_3$Cl$_3$] is a non-electrolyte — no ions released in solution, so minimum conductance. [Co(NH$_3$)$_4$Cl$_2$] similarly has no counter-ions outside the coordination sphere... Actually option 3 [Co(NH$_3$)$_3$Cl$_3$] gives zero ions, option 4 [Co(NH$_3$)$_4$Cl$_2$] also gives zero ions if neutral. Both 3 and 4 have minimum conductance. Answer: Both 3 & 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following aqueous solution will exhibit highest boiling point?
questions.solution_text: Boiling point elevation $\propto$ total particle concentration (van't Hoff factor $i \times$ molarity). Na$_2$SO$_4$: $i = 3$, effective conc. = $0.01 \times 3 = 0.03$ M. C$_6$H$_{12}$O$_6$: $i = 1$, effective = $0.015$ M. Urea: $i = 1$, effective = $0.01$ M. KNO$_3$: $i = 2$, effective = $0.02$ M. Highest: Na$_2$SO$_4$ with 0.03 M.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: SN2 reaction and leaving group ability
questions.question_text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as **Assertion (A)** and the other is labelled as **Reason (R)**. **Assertion (A):** Alkyl iodide undergoes S$_N$2 reaction faster than alkyl chloride. **Reason (R):** Iodine is a better leaving group because of its large size. In the light of the above statements, choose the **correct** answer:

options.text: Both **A** and **R** are true and **R** is the correct explanation of **A**
Both **A** and **R** are true but **R** is **not** the correct explanation of **A**

questions.solution_text: A is correct: alkyl iodide is more reactive in SN2 than alkyl chloride. R is correct: I$^-$ is a better leaving group due to large size (more polarizable, C-I bond weaker). R correctly explains A because the better leaving group ability of I$^-$ makes SN2 faster for alkyl iodides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Consider the following compounds: $\underline{K}$O$_2$, H$_2$$\underline{O}_2$ and H$_2$$\underline{S}$O$_4$. The oxidation state of the underlined elements in them are, respectively,
questions.solution_text: In KO$_2$ (potassium superoxide): $K = +1$. In H$_2$O$_2$ (hydrogen peroxide): O = $-1$. In H$_2$SO$_4$: $2(+1) + S + 4(-2) = 0$, so $S = +6$. Answer: $+1$, $-1$, $+6$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Match the industrial process with catalyst
questions.question_text:
Match **List-I** with **List-II**.

| | List-I | | List-II |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. | Haber process | I. | Fe catalyst |
| B. | Wacker oxidation | II. | PdCl$_2$ |
| C. | Wilkinson catalyst | III. | [(PPh$_3$)$_3$RhCl] |
| D. | Ziegler catalyst | IV. | TiCl$_4$ with Al(CH$_3$)$_3$ |

Choose the **correct** answer:
questions.solution_text: Haber process: Fe catalyst. Wacker oxidation (ethylene to acetaldehyde): PdCl$_2$ catalyst. Wilkinson catalyst: [(PPh$_3$)$_3$RhCl] for hydrogenation. Ziegler-Natta catalyst: TiCl$_4$ with Al(CH$_3$)$_3$ for polymerization. All match A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Given below are two statements: **Statement I:** Like nitrogen that can form ammonia, arsenic can form arsine. **Statement II:** Antimony cannot form antimony pentoxide. In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate** answer:

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I is correct: Arsenic forms arsine AsH$_3$ analogous to NH$_3$. Statement II is incorrect: Antimony (Sb) can and does form Sb$_2$O$_5$ (antimony pentoxide), as the +5 oxidation state is accessible for Sb.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Given below are two statements: **Statement I:** Ferromagnetism is considered as an extreme form of paramagnetism. **Statement II:** The number of unpaired electrons in a Cr$^{2+}$ ion (Z = 24) is the same as that of a Nd$^{3+}$ ion (Z = 60). In the light of the above statements, choose the **correct** answer:

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution_text: Statement I is true: ferromagnetism involves cooperative alignment of magnetic moments and is an extreme form of paramagnetism. Statement II: Cr$^{2+}$ is [Ar]3d$^4$, giving 4 unpaired electrons. Nd (Z=60) is [Xe]4f$^4$6s$^2$; Nd$^{3+}$ is [Xe]4f$^3$, giving 3 unpaired electrons. 4 ≠ 3, so Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which one of the following reactions does **NOT** give benzene as the product?
questions.solution_text: Option 1: Trimerization of acetylene gives benzene. Option 2: Benzene diazonium salt reacted with warm water gives phenol, NOT benzene. Option 3: Decarboxylation of sodium benzoate gives benzene. Option 4: Catalytic reforming of n-hexane gives benzene. So option 2 does NOT give benzene.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Hybridization and shape of xenon compounds
questions.question_text:
Match **List-I** with **List-II**

| | List-I | | List-II |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. | XeO$_3$ | (I) | sp$^3$d; linear |
| B. | XeF$_2$ | (II) | sp$^3$; pyramidal |
| C. | XeOF$_4$ | (III) | sp$^3$d$^3$; distorted octahedral |
| D. | XeF$_6$ | (IV) | sp$^3$d$^2$; square pyramidal |

Choose the **correct** answer:
questions.solution_text: XeO$_3$: sp$^3$, pyramidal (3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair). XeF$_2$: sp$^3$d, linear (2 bond pairs + 3 lone pairs). XeOF$_4$: sp$^3$d$^2$, square pyramidal (5 bond pairs + 1 lone pair). XeF$_6$: sp$^3$d$^3$, distorted octahedral (6 bond pairs + 1 lone pair). Match: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many products (including stereoisomers) are expected from monochlorination of the following compound? (CH$_3$)$_2$CH-CH$_2$-CH$_3$ (2-methylbutane)
questions.solution_text: 2-methylbutane positions: C1 (3H, equivalent), C2 (1H, creates chiral center → 2 enantiomers), C3 (2H, creates chiral center → 2 enantiomers), C4/methyl (3H, equivalent — same as C1-type but different position, actually C1 methyl and C4 ethyl terminal give different products). Analyzing: Cl at C1 (2-methyl-1-chlorobutane) — 1 product; Cl at C2 (2-chloro-2-methylbutane) — chiral, 2 enantiomers; Cl at C3 (2-methyl-3-chlorobutane) — chiral, 2 enantiomers; Cl at isobutyl C (1-chloro-2-methylbutane from terminal methyl groups) — those two terminal methyls are equivalent. Total = 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 6.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are true?
A. Unlike Ga that has a very high melting point, Cs has a very low melting point.
B. On Pauling scale, the electronegativity values of N and Cl are not the same.
C. Ar, K$^+$, Cl$^-$, Ca$^{2+}$, and S$^{2-}$ are all isoelectronic species.
D. The correct order of the first ionization enthalpies of Na, Mg, Al, and Si is Si > Al > Mg > Na.
E. The atomic radius of Cs is greater than that of Li and Rb.
Choose the **correct** answer the options given below:
questions.solution_text: A: False — Ga has an anomalously LOW melting point (29.7°C), not high. B: False — N and Cl both have electronegativity 3.0 on Pauling scale. C: True — all have 18 electrons. D: False — correct order is Si > Al > Na, but Mg > Al due to full s-subshell stability; actually order is Si > Mg > Al > Na. Statement D says Si > Al > Mg > Na which is incorrect (Mg > Al). E: True — Cs is the largest alkali metal, bigger than both Li and Rb. So C and E are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The standard heat of formation, in kcal/mol of Ba$^{2+}$ is: [Given: standard heat of formation of SO$_4^{2-}$ ion (aq) = $-216$ kcal/mol, standard heat of crystallisation of BaSO$_4$(s) = $-4.5$ kcal/mol, standard heat of formation of BaSO$_4$(s) = $-349$ kcal/mol]
questions.solution_text: BaSO$_4$(s) $\rightarrow$ Ba$^{2+}$(aq) + SO$_4^{2-}$(aq); $\Delta H_{dissolution} = -\Delta H_{crystallization} = +4.5$ kcal/mol. $\Delta H_f^\circ$[BaSO$_4$(s)] = $\Delta H_f^\circ$[Ba$^{2+}$] + $\Delta H_f^\circ$[SO$_4^{2-}$] $- \Delta H_{dissolution}$... Using Hess's law: $\Delta H_f^\circ$[Ba$^{2+}$] = $\Delta H_f^\circ$[BaSO$_4$(s)] $- \Delta H_f^\circ$[SO$_4^{2-}$] + $\Delta H_{dissolution}$ = $-349 - (-216) + 4.5 = -349 + 216 + 4.5 = -128.5$ kcal/mol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II

| | List-I (Example) | | List-II (Type of Solution) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. | Humidity | I. | Solid in solid |
| B. | Alloys | II. | Liquid in gas |
| C. | Amalgams | III. | Solid in gas |
| D. | Smoke | IV. | Liquid in solid |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Humidity = water vapor in air = liquid in gas (II). Alloys = solid metals mixed = solid in solid (I). Amalgams = mercury (liquid) in solid metal = liquid in solid (IV). Smoke = solid particles in gas = solid in gas (III). Match: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: C(s) + 2H$_2$(g) $\rightarrow$ CH$_4$(g); $\Delta$H = $-74.8$ kJ mol$^{-1}$. Which of the following diagrams gives an accurate representation of the above reaction? [R $\rightarrow$ reactants; P $\rightarrow$ products]

options.text: Diagram 1: P higher than R by 74.8
Diagram 2: P higher than R with hump
Diagram 3: R higher than P by 74.8 (with activation energy hump)

questions.solution_text: The reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H = -74.8$ kJ/mol), so products are at lower energy than reactants. The energy diagram should show R at higher level, an activation energy hump, then P at lower level with the difference being 74.8 kJ/mol. This corresponds to diagram 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Sugar 'X' (A) is found in honey, (B) is a keto sugar, (C) exists in $\alpha$ and $\beta$ anomeric forms, (D) Is laevorotatory. 'X' is:
questions.solution_text: D-Fructose: (A) found in honey — yes; (B) keto sugar (ketose) — yes; (C) exists in $\alpha$ and $\beta$ forms — yes; (D) laevorotatory (rotates plane polarized light to left) — yes. All four properties match D-Fructose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Total number of possible isomers (both structural as well as stereoisomers) of cyclic ethers of molecular formula C$_4$H$_8$O is:
questions.solution_text: Cyclic ethers with C$_4$H$_8$O: Oxetane rings (4-membered), Oxolane/THF (5-membered). Structural isomers and their stereoisomers: oxetane derivatives + methyloxetane + dimethyloxetane variants + tetrahydrofuran + methyloxetane isomers. Counting carefully including cis/trans and enantiomers gives 10 total isomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For the reaction A(g) $\rightleftharpoons$ 2B(g), the backward reaction rate constant is higher than the forward reaction rate constant by a factor of 2500, at 1000 K. [Given: R = 0.0831 L atm mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]. $K_P$ for the reaction at 1000 K is
questions.solution_text: $K_c = \dfrac{k_f}{k_b} = \dfrac{1}{2500} = 4 \times 10^{-4}$ mol/L. $K_P = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}$ where $\Delta n = 2-1 = 1$. $RT = 0.0831 \times 1000 = 83.1$ L·atm/mol. $K_P = 4 \times 10^{-4} \times 83.1 = 0.03324 \approx 0.033$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Ratio of wavelengths for different transitions
questions.question_text: The ratio of the wavelengths of the light absorbed by a Hydrogen atom when it undergoes $n = 2 \rightarrow n = 3$ and $n = 4 \rightarrow n = 6$ transitions, respectively, is
questions.solution_text: Using $\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R_H\left(\dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$. For $2\rightarrow 3$: $\dfrac{1}{\lambda_1} = R_H\left(\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{9}\right) = R_H \cdot \dfrac{5}{36}$. For $4\rightarrow 6$: $\dfrac{1}{\lambda_2} = R_H\left(\dfrac{1}{16} - \dfrac{1}{36}\right) = R_H \cdot \dfrac{5}{144}$. $\dfrac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2} = \dfrac{5/144}{5/36} = \dfrac{36}{144} = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Degree of dissociation from molar conductivity
questions.question_text: If the molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m$) of a 0.050 mol L$^{-1}$ solution of a monobasic weak acid is 90 S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$, its extent (degree) of dissociation will be [Assume $\Lambda_+^\circ = 349.6$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$ and $\Lambda_-^\circ = 50.4$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$]
questions.solution_text: $\Lambda_m^\circ = \Lambda_+^\circ + \Lambda_-^\circ = 349.6 + 50.4 = 400$ S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$. Degree of dissociation $\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\circ} = \dfrac{90}{400} = 0.225$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Positive and negative deviation from Raoult's law
questions.question_text: 5 moles of liquid X and 10 moles of liquid Y make a solution having a vapour pressure of 70 torr. The vapour pressures of pure X and Y are 63 torr and 78 torr respectively. Which of the following is true regarding the described solution?

options.text: The solution has volume greater than the sum of individual volumes.

questions.solution_text: Mole fraction: $x_X = 5/15 = 1/3$, $x_Y = 10/15 = 2/3$. Ideal pressure by Raoult's law: $P_{ideal} = 63 \times (1/3) + 78 \times (2/3) = 21 + 52 = 73$ torr. Actual pressure = 70 torr $< 73$ torr (ideal). Since actual VP < ideal VP, the solution shows **negative deviation** from Raoult's law.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Among the following, choose the ones with equal number of atoms.
A. 212 g of Na$_2$CO$_3$(s) [molar mass = 106 g]
B. 248 g of Na$_2$O(s) [molar mass = 62 g]
C. 240 g of NaOH(s) [molar mass = 40 g]
D. 12 g of H$_2$(g) [molar mass = 2 g]
E. 220 g of CO$_2$(g) [molar mass = 44 g]
questions.solution_text: Moles × atoms per molecule: A: 212/106 = 2 mol × 6 atoms = 12 mol atoms. B: 248/62 = 4 mol × 3 atoms = 12 mol atoms. C: 240/40 = 6 mol × 3 atoms = 18 mol atoms. D: 12/2 = 6 mol × 2 atoms = 12 mol atoms. E: 220/44 = 5 mol × 3 atoms = 15 mol atoms. A, B, D all give 12 mol atoms — equal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are paramagnetic?
A. [NiCl$_4$]$^{2-}$
B. Ni(CO)$_4$
C. [Ni(CN)$_4$]$^{2-}$
D. [Ni(H$_2$O)$_6$]$^{2+}$
E. Ni(PPh$_3$)$_4$
questions.solution_text: Ni$^{2+}$ (3d$^8$): in weak field (Cl$^-$, H$_2$O), high spin with 2 unpaired electrons (paramagnetic). In strong field (CN$^-$), low spin with 0 unpaired (diamagnetic). A: [NiCl$_4$]$^{2-}$ — tetrahedral, weak field, 2 unpaired → paramagnetic. B: Ni(CO)$_4$ — Ni(0), 3d$^{10}$, diamagnetic. C: [Ni(CN)$_4$]$^{2-}$ — square planar, strong field, paired → diamagnetic. D: [Ni(H$_2$O)$_6$]$^{2+}$ — weak field, 2 unpaired → paramagnetic. E: Ni(PPh$_3$)$_4$ — Ni(0), 3d$^{10}$, diamagnetic. Paramagnetic: A and D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Among the given compounds I-III, the correct order of bond dissociation energy of C–H bond marked with * is: [I: benzene C–H*, II: phenylacetylene C≡C–H*, III: cyclopropane C–H*]
questions.solution_text: Bond dissociation energy of C–H depends on hybridization of C: sp > sp$^2$ > sp$^3$ in terms of bond strength (s-character increases strength). I (benzene): sp$^2$ C–H. II (phenylacetylene terminal C≡C–H): sp C–H (highest s-character, strongest). III (cyclopropane): though sp$^3$, has bent bonds with higher s-character, intermediate. Order: II (sp) $>$ I (sp$^2$) $>$ III (sp$^3$-like cyclopropane but less than sp$^2$). Actually for cyclopropane: effective s-character ~33% similar to sp$^2$... Standard answer: II > I > III.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Dalton's Atomic theory could not explain which of the following?
questions.solution_text: Dalton's atomic theory successfully explained the laws of conservation of mass, constant proportion, and multiple proportions. However, it could NOT explain Gay-Lussac's Law of gaseous volumes (law of combining volumes), which required the concept of molecules (Avogadro's hypothesis).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Dipole moment, lone pairs, bond length, bond enthalpy
questions.question_text:
Identify the correct orders against the property mentioned:
A. H$_2$O $>$ NH$_3$ $>$ CHCl$_3$ – dipole moment
B. XeF$_4$ $>$ XeO$_3$ $>$ XeF$_2$ – number of lone pairs on central atom
C. O–H $>$ C–H $>$ N–O – bond length
D. N$_2$ $>$ O$_2$ $>$ H$_2$ – bond enthalpy
Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: A: Dipole moments: H$_2$O = 1.84 D, NH$_3$ = 1.47 D, CHCl$_3$ = 1.08 D. Order correct: H$_2$O > NH$_3$ > CHCl$_3$. B: Lone pairs: XeF$_4$ = 2 lp, XeO$_3$ = 1 lp, XeF$_2$ = 3 lp. Correct order should be XeF$_2$ > XeF$_4$ > XeO$_3$. Statement B is WRONG. C: Bond lengths: O–H = 96 pm, C–H = 109 pm, N–O = 122 pm. Order should be N–O > C–H > O–H. Statement C is WRONG. D: Bond enthalpies: N$_2$ = 945, O$_2$ = 498, H$_2$ = 436 kJ/mol. Order N$_2$ > O$_2$ > H$_2$ is CORRECT. So A and D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match **List-I** with **List-II**.

| | List-I (Name of Vitamin) | | List-II (Deficiency disease) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. | Vitamin B$_{12}$ | I. | Cheilosis |
| B. | Vitamin D | II. | Convulsions |
| C. | Vitamin B$_2$ | III. | Rickets |
| D. | Vitamin B$_6$ | IV. | Pernicious anaemia |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Vitamin B$_{12}$ (cobalamin) deficiency → Pernicious anaemia (IV). Vitamin D deficiency → Rickets (III). Vitamin B$_2$ (riboflavin) deficiency → Cheilosis (I). Vitamin B$_6$ (pyridoxine) deficiency → Convulsions (II). Match: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The correct order of decreasing basic strength of the given amines is:
questions.solution_text: In aqueous solution: diethylamine > ethylamine > aniline > N-methylaniline for basic strength. N-ethylethanamine (diethylamine) is most basic (two electron-donating ethyl groups + good solvation). Ethanamine (ethylamine) is next. Aromatic amines are weakest due to resonance delocalizing lone pair into ring. N-methylaniline slightly weaker than aniline due to steric hindrance. Order: N-ethylethanamine > ethanamine > N-methylaniline > benzenamine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Wavelength of light absorbed by complexes
questions.question_text:
The correct order of the wavelength of light absorbed by the following complexes is:
A. [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$
B. [Co(CN)$_6$]$^{3-}$
C. [Cu(H$_2$O)$_4$]$^{2+}$
D. [Ti(H$_2$O)$_6$]$^{3+}$
questions.solution_text: Wavelength $\lambda \propto 1/\Delta_0$ (larger crystal field splitting = shorter wavelength absorbed). Spectrochemical series: CN$^-$ $>$ NH$_3$ $>$ H$_2$O. [Co(CN)$_6$]$^{3-}$: strongest field → largest $\Delta_0$ → shortest $\lambda$. [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$: medium-strong field → medium-short $\lambda$. [Ti(H$_2$O)$_6$]$^{3+}$: Ti$^{3+}$ d$^1$, moderate $\lambda$ (visible, purple). [Cu(H$_2$O)$_4$]$^{2+}$: Cu$^{2+}$ d$^9$, weak field → longest $\lambda$ (visible blue). Order of $\lambda$: B $<$ A $<$ D $<$ C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which one of the following compounds **does not** decolourize bromine water?
questions.solution_text: Bromine water is decolourized by: alkenes (addition), aromatic amines (substitution at ring), phenols (substitution at ortho/para positions). Cyclohexane is a saturated hydrocarbon with no double bonds or activating groups — it does NOT decolourize bromine water under normal conditions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Predict the major product 'P' in the following sequence of reactions: Methylenecyclopentane (i) HBr, benzoyl peroxide (ii) KCN (iii) Na(Hg)/C$_2$H$_5$OH $\rightarrow$ P (Major)

options.text: Cyclopentane with CH$_3$ and NC at same C
Cyclopentane with NC and CH$_3$ at adjacent C
Cyclopentane with CH$_3$ and CH$_2$NH$_2$ at same C
Cyclopentane with CH$_3$ and CH$_2$NH$_2$ at ring carbon

questions.solution_text: Step 1: HBr with benzoyl peroxide (anti-Markovnikov addition) → bromo at terminal carbon (CH$_2$Br group on ring). Step 2: KCN (SN2) → CN replaces Br → CH$_2$CN. Step 3: Na/Hg in C$_2$H$_5$OH reduces CN to CH$_2$NH$_2$. Product P: cyclopentane ring with methyl and CH$_2$NH$_2$ at same ring carbon — option 3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.question_text:
Match **List I** with **List II**

| | List-I (Mixture) | | List-II (Method of separation) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. | CHCl$_3$ + C$_6$H$_5$NH$_2$ | (I) | Distillation under reduced pressure |
| B. | Crude oil in petroleum industry | (II) | Steam distillation |
| C. | Glycerol from spent-lye | (III) | Fractional distillation |
| D. | Aniline - water | (IV) | Simple distillation |
questions.solution_text: CHCl$_3$ + aniline (close boiling points) → simple distillation (IV) works if bp differ enough, but actually fractional. Crude oil → fractional distillation (III). Glycerol from spent-lye (high bp, decomposes on heating) → distillation under reduced pressure (I). Aniline-water (immiscible, different bp) → steam distillation (II). Match: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which among the following electronic configurations belong to main group elements?
A. [Ne]3s$^1$
B. [Ar]3d$^3$4s$^2$
C. [Kr]4d$^{10}$5s$^2$5p$^5$
D. [Ar]3d$^{10}$4s$^1$
E. [Rn]5f$^0$6d$^2$7s$^2$
questions.solution_text: Main group elements have outermost electrons in s or p orbitals (groups 1, 2, 13-18). A: [Ne]3s$^1$ — Group 1 (Na), main group. B: [Ar]3d$^3$4s$^2$ — d-block (V), not main group. C: [Kr]4d$^{10}$5s$^2$5p$^5$ — p-block (I/halogen), main group. D: [Ar]3d$^{10}$4s$^1$ — d-block (Cu), not main group. E: [Rn]5f$^0$6d$^2$7s$^2$ — d-block (Rf), not main group. Main group: A and C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which one of the following compounds can exist as cis-trans isomers?
questions.solution_text: For cis-trans isomerism in cyclic compounds, two different carbons in the ring each need two different substituents. In 1,2-dimethylcyclohexane, C1 has (H, CH$_3$) and C2 has (H, CH$_3$) — both carbons have two different groups, enabling cis-trans isomerism. 1,1-dimethylcyclopropane has two identical groups on C1, so no cis-trans. Pent-1-ene: CH$_2$=CH-C$_3$H$_7$ — terminal alkene (one carbon has two H), no geometric isomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Phosphoric acid ionizes in three steps with their ionization constant values $K_{a_1}$, $K_{a_2}$ and $K_{a_3}$, respectively, while $K$ is the overall ionization constant. Which of the following statements are true?
A. $\log K = \log K_{a_1} + \log K_{a_2} + \log K_{a_3}$
B. H$_3$PO$_4$ is a stronger acid than H$_2$PO$_4^-$ and HPO$_4^{2-}$
C. $K_{a_1} > K_{a_2} > K_{a_3}$
D. $K_{a_1} = \dfrac{K_{a_3} > K_{a_2}}{2}$
questions.solution_text: A: True — $K = K_{a_1} \times K_{a_2} \times K_{a_3}$, so $\log K = \log K_{a_1} + \log K_{a_2} + \log K_{a_3}$. B: True — H$_3$PO$_4$ is easier to donate first proton; successive ionization becomes harder as negative charge increases. C: True — successive ionization constants decrease: $K_{a_1} > K_{a_2} > K_{a_3}$. D: False — $K_{a_1} \neq (K_{a_3} > K_{a_2})/2$; this is an arbitrary and incorrect statement. A, B, C are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match **List I** with **List II**

| | List-I (Ion) | | List-II (Group Number in Cation Analysis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. | Co$^{2+}$ | I. | Group-I |
| B. | Mg$^{2+}$ | II. | Group-III |
| C. | Pb$^{2+}$ | III. | Group-IV |
