Choose the **correct** answer:
questions.solution_text: Co$^{2+}$ precipitates in Group III (as CoS). Mg$^{2+}$ precipitates in Group VI (as Mg(OH)$_2$). Pb$^{2+}$ precipitates in Group I (as PbCl$_2$) and also Group II. Al$^{3+}$ precipitates in Group III (as Al(OH)$_3$). Match: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Conditions for higher yield of NO
questions.question_text:
Higher yield of NO in N$_2$(g) + O$_2$(g) $\rightleftharpoons$ 2NO(g) can be obtained at [$\Delta H$ of the reaction = +180.7 kJ mol$^{-1}$]
A. Higher temperature
B. Lower temperature
C. Higher concentration of N$_2$
D. Higher concentration of O$_2$
questions.solution_text: The reaction is endothermic ($\Delta H > 0$), so higher temperature shifts equilibrium to right (more NO). $\Delta n = 0$ (2 moles both sides), so pressure doesn't affect yield. Higher concentration of N$_2$ or O$_2$ shifts equilibrium right (more NO). A, C, D are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Preparation and properties of diazonium salts
questions.question_text: Given below are two statements: **Statement-I:** Benzenediazonium salt is prepared by the reaction of aniline with nitrous acid at 273–278 K. It decomposes easily in the dry state. **Statement-II:** Insertion of iodine into the benzene ring is difficult and hence iodobenzene is prepared through the reaction of benzenediazonium salt with KI. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I is correct: benzenediazonium chloride is prepared at 273-278 K by diazotization and decomposes on heating or when dry. Statement II is correct: direct iodination of benzene is difficult (I$_2$ is a poor electrophile for benzene), so iodobenzene is made via Sandmeyer-like reaction using diazonium salt + KI.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The major product of the following reaction is: [PhCH$_2$COCN + (i) CH$_3$MgBr (excess) (ii) H$_3$O$^+$]

options.text: Ph with OH, OH, CH$_3$, CH$_3$ substituents
Ph with ketone and ester groups
Ph with OH and CN groups
Ph with OH and methyl ketone

questions.solution_text: PhCH$_2$COCN has both a ketone (C=O) and nitrile (CN) group. CH$_3$MgBr (excess) first attacks the more reactive ketone C=O → after workup gives alcohol. The CN reacts with second equivalent of CH$_3$MgBr to form an imine, which hydrolyzes to a methyl ketone. Major product: Ph-CH(OH)-C(CH$_3$)=O (with OH on benzylic carbon and methyl ketone). This matches option 4.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the above represented plasmid, an alien piece of DNA is inserted at EcoRI site. Which of the following strategies will be chosen to select the recombinant colonies? [Plasmid has: BamH1, Tet R, EcoRI, β-Galactosidase, amp (ampicillin resistance), Ori]

options.text: White color colonies will be selected.
Blue color colonies grown on ampicillin plates can be selected.
Using ampicillin & tetracyclin containing medium plate.
Blue color colonies will be selected.

questions.solution_text: The alien DNA is inserted at EcoRI site, which is within the β-galactosidase gene. Insertional inactivation of β-galactosidase means recombinants cannot hydrolyze X-gal → colonies remain white. Non-recombinants with intact β-galactosidase → blue colonies. The plasmid retains amp$^R$ (ampicillin resistance not disrupted). White colonies = recombinants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The protein portion of an enzyme is called:
questions.solution_text: The protein portion of a conjugated enzyme (holoenzyme) is called the apoenzyme. The non-protein part is the cofactor. Together, apoenzyme + cofactor = holoenzyme.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Given below are two statements: **Statement I:** The primary source of energy in an ecosystem is solar energy. **Statement II:** The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis in an ecosystem is called net primary productivity (NPP). In the light of the above statements, choose the **most appropriate** answer:

options.text: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I is correct: solar energy is the primary source of energy in most ecosystems. Statement II is incorrect: the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis is called **Gross** Primary Productivity (GPP). Net Primary Productivity (NPP) = GPP minus respiration losses (NPP = GPP - R).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as **Assertion (A)** and the other is labelled as **Reason (R)**. **Assertion (A):** A typical unfertilised, angiosperm embryo sac at maturity is 8 nucleate and 7-celled. **Reason (R):** The egg apparatus has 2 polar nuclei. In the light of the above statements, choose the **correct** answer:

options.text: Both **A** and **R** are true and **R** is the correct explanation of **A**
Both **A** and **R** are true but **R** is **NOT** the correct explanation of **A**

questions.solution_text: A is true: mature embryo sac has 8 nuclei and 7 cells (3 antipodals + 2 synergids + 1 egg cell + 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei). R is false: the 2 polar nuclei are in the central cell, NOT in the egg apparatus. The egg apparatus consists of 1 egg cell + 2 synergids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Neoplastic characteristics of cells refer to:
A. A mass of proliferating cell
B. Rapid growth of cells
C. Invasion and damage to the surrounding tissue
D. Those confined to original location
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Neoplastic characteristics include: A mass of proliferating cells (A), rapid growth of cells (B), and invasion and damage to surrounding tissue (C). Option D is incorrect — neoplastic (malignant) cells are NOT confined to the original location; they invade surrounding tissues and metastasize. Benign tumors are confined, not neoplastic/malignant ones.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which one of the following is the characteristic feature of gymnosperms?
questions.solution_text: The defining characteristic of gymnosperms is that their seeds are naked (not enclosed in a fruit/ovary). The word 'gymnosperm' itself means 'naked seed' (gymno = naked, sperma = seed). They do not have flowers, do not enclose seeds in fruits, and do produce seeds.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I: A. Progesterone, B. Relaxin, C. Melanocyte stimulating hormone, D. Catecholamines
List-II: I. Pars intermedia, II. Ovary, III. Adrenal Medulla, IV. Corpus luteum

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Progesterone is secreted by Corpus luteum (IV). Relaxin is secreted by Ovary (II). Melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH) is secreted by Pars intermedia of pituitary (I). Catecholamines (adrenaline, noradrenaline) are secreted by Adrenal Medulla (III). Match: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Chromosome with highest number of genes
questions.question_text: Which chromosome in the human genome has the highest number of genes?
questions.solution_text: Chromosome 1 is the largest human chromosome and contains the highest number of genes (~2000 genes). This was established by the Human Genome Project. Chromosome Y has the fewest genes among the sex chromosomes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about RuBisCo is true?

options.text: It is an enzyme involved in the photolysis of water
It catalyzes the carboxylation of RuBP
It is active only in the dark
It has higher affinity for oxygen than carbon dioxide

questions.solution_text: RuBisCO (Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase) catalyzes the carboxylation of RuBP (Ribulose bisphosphate) during the Calvin cycle — the first step of carbon fixation. It is active in light (not dark). It actually has higher affinity for CO2 than O2, though it can use both. It is not involved in photolysis of water.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The first menstruation is called:
questions.solution_text: Menarche refers to the first menstrual cycle/first menstruation in a female's life, typically occurring at puberty. Menopause is the cessation of menstruation. Ovulation is the release of an egg. Diapause is a period of suspended development in insects.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following genetically engineered organisms was used by Eli Lilly to prepare human insulin?
questions.solution_text: Eli Lilly, an American pharmaceutical company, first used genetically engineered Escherichia coli (bacterium) to produce human insulin in 1982. The insulin gene was inserted into E. coli plasmids. The two chains (A and B) were produced separately in bacteria and then combined to form functional insulin (Humulin).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrate.
Reason (R): The members of subphylum vertebrata possess notochord during the embryonic period, the notochord is replaced by cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in adults.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

questions.solution_text: A is true: Vertebrata is a subphylum of Chordata, so all vertebrates are chordates but not all chordates are vertebrates (e.g., Urochordata and Cephalochordata are chordates but not vertebrates). R is true: Vertebrates possess notochord only during embryonic period, which is later replaced by vertebral column. R correctly explains why vertebrates are a subset of chordates — they are defined by having a vertebral column replacing the notochord.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: What is the main function of the spindle fibers during mitosis?
questions.solution_text: Spindle fibers (made of tubulin proteins) form the mitotic spindle apparatus. Their main function is to separate (pull apart) the chromosomes during anaphase of mitosis, moving sister chromatids to opposite poles of the cell. DNA repair occurs in interphase, DNA synthesis in S phase, and cell growth regulation involves other mechanisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II:
A. Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase — B. Euchromatin — C. Frederick Griffith — D. Heterochromatin
I. Streptococcus pneumoniae — II. Densely packed and dark-stained — III. Loosely packed and light-stained — IV. DNA as genetic material confirmation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase confirmed DNA as genetic material (IV) using bacteriophage T2 experiment. Euchromatin is loosely packed and light-stained (III) — transcriptionally active. Frederick Griffith worked with Streptococcus pneumoniae (I) in his transformation experiment. Heterochromatin is densely packed and dark-stained (II) — transcriptionally inactive. Match: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II:
A. Adenosine — B. Adenylic acid — C. Adenine — D. Alanine
I. Nitrogen base — II. Nucleotide — III. Nucleoside — IV. Amino acid
Choose the option with all correct matches.
questions.solution_text: Adenosine = Adenine + Ribose sugar = Nucleoside (III). Adenylic acid = Adenosine + Phosphate = Nucleotide (II). Adenine = Nitrogen base (purine) (I). Alanine = Amino acid (IV). Match: A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In frog, the Renal portal system is a special venous connection that acts to link:

options.text: Kidney and lower part of body

questions.solution_text: In frogs, the renal portal system consists of veins that carry blood from the lower part of the body (hind limbs, tail region) directly to the kidneys for filtration before returning to general circulation. It links the kidney with the lower part of the body (posterior region).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are the post-transcriptional events in an eukaryotic cell?
A. Transport of pre-mRNA to cytoplasm prior to splicing.
B. Removal of introns and joining of exons.
C. Addition of methyl group at 5' end of hnRNA.
D. Addition of adenine residues at 3' end of hnRNA.
E. Base pairing of two complementary RNAs.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Post-transcriptional processing in eukaryotes includes: B. Splicing (removal of introns, joining of exons); C. 5' capping — addition of 7-methylguanosine cap (methyl group addition); D. 3' polyadenylation — addition of poly-A tail (adenine residues). A is incorrect — splicing occurs in nucleus before transport. E is not a standard post-transcriptional processing event of hnRNA. Answer: B, C, D only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplifies DNA following the equation.
questions.solution_text: In PCR, after n cycles, the number of DNA copies produced is 2ⁿ (2 to the power n). Each cycle doubles the number of DNA molecules. After 1 cycle: 2 copies; after 2 cycles: 4 copies; after 30 cycles: 2³⁰ copies (approximately 1 billion copies).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Both wind and water pollinated flowers are not very colourful and do not produce nectar.
Reason (R): The flowers produce enormous amount of pollen grains in wind and water pollinated flowers.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

questions.solution_text: A is true: Wind and water pollinated flowers are generally not colourful and do not produce nectar, as they do not need to attract pollinators. R is true: Wind-pollinated flowers produce enormous amounts of pollen grains (to compensate for the random nature of wind dispersal). However, R does not explain A — the lack of color and nectar is because attracting insects/animals is unnecessary, not because of large pollen production. These are two separate adaptations.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Epiphytes that are growing on a mango branch is an example of which of the following?
questions.solution_text: Epiphytes (plants growing on other plants for physical support, like orchids on a mango tree) are examples of commensalism (+/0 interaction). The epiphyte benefits by getting support and better access to sunlight, while the mango tree is neither harmed nor benefited. This is the classic example of commensalism.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Find the correct statement:
A. In human pregnancy, the major organ systems are formed at the end of 12 weeks.
B. In human pregnancy the major organ systems are formed at the end of 8 weeks.
C. In human pregnancy heart is formed after one month of gestation.
D. In human pregnancy, limbs and digits develop by the end of second month.
E. In human pregnancy the appearance of hair is usually observed in the fifth month.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: B, C, D and E only
A, C, D and E only

questions.solution_text: A is correct: Major organ systems are formed by end of 12 weeks (first trimester). B is incorrect (8 weeks is wrong — it's 12 weeks for major systems). C is correct: Heart is formed after ~1 month of gestation. D is correct: Limbs and digits develop by end of second month. E is correct: Hair appears around the 5th month. Correct statements: A, C, D, E.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Identify the part of a bio-reactor which is used as a foam breaker from the given figure. [Figure shows bioreactor with parts labeled A, B, C, D]
questions.solution_text: In a bioreactor diagram, the foam breaker is typically located near the top of the vessel. From the figure described, part C represents the foam breaker. Foam breakers are used to break foam that forms during fermentation, which could otherwise reduce efficiency and contaminate the product.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Frogs respire in water by skin and buccal cavity and on land by skin, buccal cavity and lungs. Choose the correct answer from the following:

options.text: The statement is false for water but true for land
The statement is false for both the environment
The statement is true for water but false for land
The statement is true for both the environment

questions.solution_text: In water, frogs respire only through skin (cutaneous respiration) — the buccal cavity is NOT used for respiration in water. On land, frogs use skin, buccal cavity, and lungs for respiration. So the statement about water respiration is false (buccal cavity not used in water), but the statement about land respiration is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding function of adrenal medullary hormones:
A. It causes pupilary constriction.
B. It is a hyperglycemic hormone.
C. It causes piloerection.
D. It increases strength of heart contraction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Adrenal medullary hormones (adrenaline/epinephrine and noradrenaline) are 'fight or flight' hormones. They: B. Are hyperglycemic (raise blood glucose by glycogenolysis); C. Cause piloerection (hair standing); D. Increase heart rate and strength of contraction. A is INCORRECT — they cause pupilary DILATION (mydriasis), not constriction, to improve vision during emergency. So B, C, D are correct.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Read the following statements on plant growth and development.
A. Parthenocarpy can be induced by auxins.
B. Plant growth regulators can be involved in promotion as well as inhibition of growth.
C. Dedifferentiation is a pre-requisite for re-differentiation.
D. Abscisic acid is a plant growth promoter.
E. Apical dominance promotes the growth of lateral buds.
Choose the option with all correct statements.
questions.solution_text: A is correct: Auxins can induce parthenocarpy (fruit development without fertilization). B is correct: PGRs can both promote (auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins) and inhibit (ABA, ethylene) growth. C is correct: Dedifferentiation (mature cells becoming meristematic) is a prerequisite for re-differentiation (forming new structures). D is incorrect: ABA (Abscisic acid) is a growth INHIBITOR, not promoter. E is incorrect: Apical dominance INHIBITS (suppresses) lateral bud growth, not promotes it.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following hormones released from the pituitary is actually synthesized in the hypothalamus?
questions.solution_text: ADH (Anti-diuretic hormone/Vasopressin) and Oxytocin are synthesized in the hypothalamus but stored and released from the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis). FSH, LH, and ACTH are synthesized and released by the anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis) under control of hypothalamic releasing hormones.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of non-distilled alcoholic beverage produced by yeast?
questions.solution_text: Beer and wine are non-distilled alcoholic beverages produced by fermentation by Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast). Rum, whisky, and brandy are distilled beverages — they undergo an additional distillation step after fermentation to increase alcohol content.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Pattern of inheritance for polygenic trait
questions.question_text: What is the pattern of inheritance for polygenic trait?
questions.solution_text: Polygenic inheritance (e.g., skin color, height) involves multiple genes each contributing additively to a single trait. It follows a non-Mendelian pattern because it does not show simple dominant-recessive ratios. Instead, it produces a continuous range of phenotypes with a bell-shaped distribution in the population.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Parts of sperm and their functions
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
A. Head — B. Middle piece — C. Acrosome — D. Tail
(i) Enzymes — (ii) Sperm motility — (iii) Energy — (iv) Genetic material
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Head of sperm contains the nucleus with genetic material (iv). Middle piece contains mitochondria that provide energy (iii) for movement. Acrosome (cap-like structure on head) contains hydrolytic enzymes (i) for penetrating the egg. Tail provides sperm motility (ii). Match: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a zygomorphic flower?
questions.solution_text: Zygomorphic flowers can be divided into two equal halves by only ONE plane of symmetry (bilaterally symmetrical). Pea (Pisum sativum) has a zygomorphic/irregular flower (papilionaceous corolla). Chilli, Petunia, and Datura have actinomorphic (radially symmetrical) flowers that can be divided into equal halves by multiple planes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of following organisms cannot fix nitrogen?
A. Azotobacter
B. Oscillatoria
C. Anabaena
D. Volvox
E. Nostoc
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Volvox (D) is a green algae (Chlorophyta) that CANNOT fix nitrogen. Azotobacter (A) is a free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium. Oscillatoria (B), Anabaena (C), and Nostoc (E) are all cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) that can fix nitrogen (Anabaena and Nostoc have heterocysts for nitrogen fixation; Oscillatoria also fixes nitrogen). Volvox lacks the machinery for nitrogen fixation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
questions.solution_text: Ex-situ conservation means conservation outside the natural habitat. Zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks, and wildlife safari parks are examples of ex-situ conservation. Protected areas, National Parks, and Wildlife Sanctuaries are examples of in-situ conservation (conservation within the natural habitat).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Who is known as the father of Ecology in India?
questions.solution_text: Ramdeo Misra is known as the 'Father of Ecology in India'. He founded the school of ecology in India and made significant contributions to plant ecology. Birbal Sahni is known for paleobotany. S.R. Kashyap is known for bryology.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: RNA as first genetic material and DNA evolution
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In the RNA world, RNA is considered the first genetic material evolved to carry out essential life processes. RNA acts as a genetic material and also as a catalyst for some important biochemical reactions in living systems. Being reactive, RNA is unstable.
Statement II: DNA evolved from RNA and is a more stable genetic material. Its double helical strands being complementary, resist changes by evolving repairing mechanism.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect

questions.solution_text: Both statements are correct. Statement I correctly describes the RNA world hypothesis — RNA was the first genetic material, acts as both genetic material and catalyst (ribozymes), but is chemically reactive and unstable due to the 2'-OH group. Statement II correctly states that DNA evolved from RNA and is more stable due to deoxyribose sugar, and its double-stranded complementary nature allows for DNA repair mechanisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Transfer RNAs and ribosomal RNA do not interact with mRNA.
Statement II: RNA interference (RNAi) takes place in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I is incorrect: tRNA and rRNA DO interact with mRNA during translation — tRNA brings amino acids and recognizes codons on mRNA through anticodon-codon pairing; rRNA (as part of ribosome) facilitates this interaction. Statement II is correct: RNAi (RNA interference) is a mechanism of gene silencing/cellular defence that occurs in all eukaryotic organisms through double-stranded RNA molecules.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
A. Heart — B. Kidney — C. Gastro-intestinal tract — D. Adrenal Cortex
(i) Erythropoietin — (ii) Aldosterone — (iii) Atrial natriuretic factor — (iv) Secretin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Heart secretes Atrial Natriuretic Factor/ANF (iii) — regulates blood pressure. Kidney secretes Erythropoietin (i) — stimulates RBC production. Gastro-intestinal tract secretes Secretin (iv) — stimulates pancreatic secretion. Adrenal Cortex secretes Aldosterone (ii) — regulates sodium reabsorption. Match: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: All living members of the class Cyclostomata are:
questions.solution_text: All living cyclostomes (lampreys and hagfish) are ectoparasites. They attach to the body of other fish using their sucking disc-like mouth and feed on their body fluids and tissues from the outside. They are not endoparasites (internal) or free-living.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Streptokinase produced by bacterium Streptococcus is used for:
questions.solution_text: Streptokinase is a 'clot buster' enzyme produced by Streptococcus bacteria. It is used as a thrombolytic agent to dissolve/remove blood clots from blocked blood vessels (e.g., in heart attacks and strokes). It activates plasminogen to plasmin which breaks down fibrin clots.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Role of the water vascular system in Echinoderms is:
A. Respiration and Locomotion
B. Excretion and Locomotion
C. Capture and transport of food
D. Digestion and Respiration
E. Digestion and Excretion
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: The water vascular system in echinoderms (e.g., starfish) functions in: A. Locomotion (tube feet movement) and Respiration (gas exchange through tube feet/papulae); C. Capture and transport of food (tube feet help grasp prey and move food to mouth). It does not perform excretion or digestion directly. Answer: A and C only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
A. Pteridophyte — B. Bryophyte — C. Angiosperm — D. Gymnosperm
(i) Salvia — (ii) Ginkgo — (iii) Polytrichum — (iv) Salvinia
Choose the option with all correct matches.
questions.solution_text: Salvinia (iv) is a Pteridophyte (water fern). Polytrichum (iii) is a Bryophyte (moss). Salvia (i) is an Angiosperm (flowering plant, family Lamiaceae). Ginkgo (ii) is a Gymnosperm (Ginkgophyta). Match: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which are correct:
A. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging detect cancers of internal organs.
B. Chemotherapeutics drugs are used to kill non-cancerous cells.
C. α-interferon activate the cancer patients' immune system and helps in destroying the tumour.
D. Chemotherapeutic drugs are biological response modifiers.
E. In the case of leukaemia blood cell counts are decreased.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: A is correct: CT scans and MRI are used to detect internal organ cancers. B is incorrect: Chemotherapeutic drugs target rapidly dividing cells (primarily cancer cells, though they also affect some normal cells as side effects). C is correct: Alpha-interferons are biological response modifiers that activate the immune system to destroy tumour cells. D is incorrect: Biological response modifiers include interferons, interleukins etc., not chemotherapeutic drugs which are chemicals. E is incorrect: In leukaemia (blood cancer), white blood cell counts are typically greatly INCREASED. Answer: A and C.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
What are the potential drawbacks in adoption of the IVF method?
A. High fatality risk to mother
B. Expensive instruments and reagents
C. Husband/wife necessary for being donors
D. Less adoption of orphans
E. Not available in India
F. Possibility that the early embryo does not survive
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A, B, C, E, F only

questions.solution_text: Drawbacks of IVF: B. It requires expensive instruments and reagents (financially inaccessible for many); D. It reduces adoption of orphans as couples prefer biological children; F. Early embryo may not survive after transfer. A is incorrect — IVF does not carry high fatality risk to mother (it is relatively safe). C is incorrect — donors need not be husband/wife (donor eggs/sperm can be used). E is incorrect — IVF is available in India. Answer: B, D, F.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Comparison of male and female gametogenesis
questions.question_text:
Consider the following:
A. The reductive division for the human female gametogenesis starts earlier than that of the male gametogenesis.
B. The gap between the first meiotic division and the second meiotic division is much shorter for males compared to females.
C. The first polar body is associated with the formation of the primary oocyte.
D. Luteinizing Hormone (LH) surge leads to disintegration of the endometrium and onset of menstrual bleeding.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: A is true: Female meiosis begins before birth (fetal life), while male meiosis begins at puberty — so female reductive division starts much earlier. B is true: In males, meiosis I and II occur in quick succession (continuous spermatogenesis). In females, there is a long arrest between meiosis I (completed just before ovulation) and meiosis II (completed only after fertilization) — gap is much longer for females. C is incorrect: The first polar body is produced at completion of meiosis I (from secondary oocyte formation, not primary oocyte). D is incorrect: LH surge triggers ovulation, not menstrual bleeding; withdrawal of progesterone/estrogen causes menstrual bleeding.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In bryophytes, the gemmae help in which one of the following?
questions.solution_text: Gemmae are small, lens-shaped, multicellular asexual reproductive structures found in bryophytes (e.g., Marchantia). They are produced in gemma cups on the thallus and when dispersed by rain splash, they develop into new gametophytes — this is a form of asexual (vegetative) reproduction.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A), and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The primary function of the Golgi apparatus is to package the materials made by the endoplasmic reticulum and deliver it to intracellular targets and outside the cell.
Reason (R): Vesicles containing materials made by the endoplasmic reticulum fuse with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus, and they are modified and released from the trans face of the Golgi apparatus.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

questions.solution_text: A is true: The primary function of Golgi apparatus is packaging, modifying, and delivering materials (proteins, lipids) to intracellular targets and for secretion. R is true: ER vesicles do fuse with the cis face (entry face) and materials are processed and exit from the trans face (exit face). However, R is NOT the correct explanation of A — R describes the mechanism/process of how materials flow through Golgi, not the primary function (packaging and delivery). The function and mechanism are separate aspects.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements refers to Reductionist Biology?

options.text: Chemical approach to study and understand living organisms
Behavioural approach to study and understand living organisms
Physico-chemical approach to study and understand living organisms
Physiological approach to study and understand living organisms

questions.solution_text: Reductionist Biology refers to the approach of studying living organisms by reducing them to their physico-chemical components and processes. It involves understanding life at the molecular, atomic, and chemical level — analyzing living things in terms of physics and chemistry (physico-chemical approach).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
After maturation, in primary lymphoid organs, the lymphocytes migrate for interaction with antigens to secondary lymphoid organ(s)/tissue(s) like:
A. thymus
B. bone marrow
C. spleen
D. lymph nodes
E. Peyer's patches
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Primary lymphoid organs (where lymphocytes mature): Thymus (A) and Bone marrow (B). Secondary lymphoid organs (where mature lymphocytes interact with antigens): Spleen (C), Lymph nodes (D), Peyer's patches in intestine (E), tonsils, MALT. After maturing in thymus/bone marrow, lymphocytes migrate to secondary lymphoid organs to encounter antigens. Answer: C, D, E only.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II:
A. The Evil Quartet — B. Ex situ conservation — C. Lantana camara — D. Dodo
I. Cryopreservation — II. Alien species invasion — III. Causes of biodiversity losses — IV. Extinction
Choose the option with all correct matches.
questions.solution_text: The Evil Quartet = four major causes of biodiversity losses (III). Ex situ conservation includes cryopreservation, seed banks, zoos (I). Lantana camara = an invasive/alien species (II). Dodo = extinct bird, example of extinction (IV). Match: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: How many meiotic and mitotic divisions need to occur for the development of a mature female gametophyte from the megaspore mother cell in an angiosperm plant?
questions.solution_text: From megaspore mother cell (MMC): 1 meiosis produces 4 megaspores (only 1 functional). Then the functional megaspore undergoes 3 mitotic divisions to produce 8 nuclei → 7-celled embryo sac. First mitosis: 2 nuclei; Second mitosis: 4 nuclei; Third mitosis: 8 nuclei. Total: 1 meiosis + 3 mitosis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following type of immunity is present at the time of birth and is a non-specific type of defence in the human body?
questions.solution_text: Innate immunity is the non-specific defence mechanism present from birth. It includes physical barriers (skin, mucus), physiological barriers (fever, stomach acid), cellular barriers (phagocytes), and cytokine barriers. It does not require prior exposure to an antigen. Acquired immunity (cell-mediated and humoral) is specific and develops after exposure to antigens.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Fig fruit is a non-vegetarian fruit as it has enclosed fig wasps in it.
Statement II: Fig wasp and fig tree exhibit mutual relationship as fig wasp completes its life cycle in fig fruit and fig fruit gets pollinated by fig wasp.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I is incorrect: While figs may contain dead fig wasps, this does not make them 'non-vegetarian' in the biological/dietary sense — the claim is misleading/incorrect as conventionally understood. Statement II is incorrect: The relationship is indeed mutualistic (fig provides breeding site for wasp; wasp pollinates fig) but saying fig 'fruit' gets pollinated is wrong — it is the fig flower/inflorescence that gets pollinated, not the fruit. Both statements have inaccuracies.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Cells of the tapetum possess dense cytoplasm and generally have more than one nucleus.
Reason (R): Presence of more than one nucleus in the tapetum increases the efficiency of nourishing the developing microspore mother cells.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

questions.solution_text: A is true: Tapetum cells do have dense cytoplasm and are often binucleate or polyploid (more than one nucleus) — this is a well-established fact. R is false: The tapetum nourishes developing microspores (not microspore mother cells — the mother cells undergo meiosis to form microspores). The tapetum provides nutrition to developing pollen grains/microspores, not to the mother cells per se. The reason incorrectly identifies the target of nourishment.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
From the statements given below choose the correct option:
A. The eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S and prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S.
B. Each ribosome has two sub-units.
C. The two sub-units of 80S ribosome are 60S and 40S while that of 70S are 50S and 30S.
D. The two sub-units of 80S ribosome are 60S and 20S and that of 70S are 50S and 20S.
E. The two sub-units of 80S are 60S and 30S and that of 70S are 50S and 30S.
questions.solution_text: A is correct: Eukaryotic ribosomes = 80S; Prokaryotic = 70S. B is correct: Each ribosome has two subunits (large and small). C is correct: 80S ribosome has 60S (large) + 40S (small) subunits; 70S ribosome has 50S (large) + 30S (small) subunits. D is incorrect (wrong subunit sizes). E is incorrect (80S does NOT have 30S subunit). Answer: A, B, C.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following enzymes contains 'Haem' as the prosthetic group?
questions.solution_text: Catalase contains haem (iron-containing porphyrin) as its prosthetic group. It catalyzes the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen. Succinate dehydrogenase has FAD as prosthetic group. RuBisCO has Mg²⁺. Carbonic anhydrase contains Zn²⁺ as cofactor.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: What is the name of the blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart in a frog?
questions.solution_text: Vena cava (precaval and postcaval veins) carries deoxygenated blood from the body tissues back to the heart (sinus venosus → right atrium) in frogs. Pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs. Pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from lungs to heart. Aorta carries oxygenated blood from heart to body.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are the stages in the life cycle of pteridophytes. Arrange the following stages in the correct sequence.
A. Prothallus stage
B. Meiosis in spore mother cells
C. Fertilisation
D. Formation of archegonia and antheridia in gametophyte.
E. Transfer of antherozoids to the archegonia in presence of water.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Correct sequence in pteridophyte life cycle: B (Meiosis in spore mother cells → forms spores) → A (Spores germinate to form Prothallus/gametophyte) → D (Formation of archegonia and antheridia on prothallus) → E (Antherozoids released and transferred to archegonia in water) → C (Fertilisation → zygote → sporophyte). Sequence: B, A, D, E, C.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Recombinant vs non-recombinant in blue-white selection
questions.question_text:
The blue and white selectable markers have been developed which differentiate recombinant colonies from non-recombinant colonies on the basis of their ability to produce colour in the presence of a chromogenic substrate.
Statement I: The blue coloured colonies have DNA insert in the plasmid and they are identified as recombinant colonies.
Statement II: The colonies without blue colour have DNA insert in the plasmid and are identified as recombinant colonies.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I is incorrect: Blue colonies have an INTACT lacZ gene (no insert), so β-galactosidase is produced → hydrolyzes X-gal → blue color. These are NON-recombinant. Statement II is correct: Colonies WITHOUT blue color (white colonies) have a DNA insert disrupting the lacZ gene (insertional inactivation) → no β-galactosidase → no color from X-gal. These white colonies ARE the recombinants.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Microbes NOT involved in household products
questions.question_text:
Which of the following microbes is NOT involved in the preparation of household products?
A. Aspergillus niger
B. Lactobacillus
C. Trichoderma polysporum
D. Saccharomyces cerevisiae
E. Propionibacterium sharmanii
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Household products involve: Lactobacillus (B) — curd/yogurt; Saccharomyces cerevisiae (D) — bread (fermentation); Propionibacterium sharmanii (E) — Swiss cheese (CO₂ holes). NOT household: Aspergillus niger (A) — used industrially for citric acid production; Trichoderma polysporum (C) — produces cyclosporin A (immunosuppressant drug), not household. Answer: A and C only.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Silencing of specific mRNA is possible via RNAi because of
questions.solution_text: RNA interference (RNAi) involves double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) that is complementary to the target mRNA. The dsRNA is processed into small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) by Dicer enzyme. The siRNA then guides the RISC complex to the complementary mRNA, leading to its degradation and gene silencing. So complementary dsRNA is the mechanism.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The complex II of mitochondrial electron transport chain is also known as
questions.solution_text: Complex II of the mitochondrial electron transport chain is Succinate dehydrogenase (SDH). It oxidizes succinate to fumarate in the Krebs cycle and passes electrons to ubiquinone (CoQ). Complex I = NADH dehydrogenase; Complex III = Cytochrome bc1 complex; Complex IV = Cytochrome c oxidase.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: While trying to find out the characteristic of a newly found animal, a researcher did the histology of adult animal and observed a cavity with presence of mesodermal tissue towards the body wall but no mesodermal tissue was observed towards the alimentary canal. What could be the possible coelome of that animal?
questions.solution_text: A pseudocoelom is a body cavity that is NOT lined by mesoderm on both sides. In pseudocoelomates, the body cavity is lined by mesoderm only on the outer side (body wall) but the inner side (alimentary canal/gut) is NOT lined by mesoderm. This matches the description: mesoderm present towards body wall but absent towards alimentary canal. Examples: Nematoda (roundworms).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In a floral formula ⊕ stands for zygomorphic nature of the flower, and G stands for inferior ovary.
Statement II: In a floral formula ⊕ stands for actinomorphic nature of the flower and G stands for superior ovary.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I is incorrect: ⊕ (or *) stands for ACTINOMORPHIC (radially symmetrical), not zygomorphic. Zygomorphic is represented by % symbol. Also, G with a line above it represents inferior ovary (ovary below), while G without line or with line below represents superior ovary. Statement II is correct: ⊕ represents actinomorphic nature. For G symbols: conventionally, G with overline = inferior ovary; plain G = superior ovary.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In ecosystem, there is unidirectional flow of energy of sun from producers to consumers.
Statement II: Ecosystems are exempted from 2nd law of thermodynamics.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I is correct: Energy flow in an ecosystem is unidirectional — from sun to producers (photosynthesis) to herbivores to carnivores, and is not recycled. Statement II is incorrect: Ecosystems do NOT violate or are NOT exempt from the 2nd law of thermodynamics. Energy is lost as heat at each trophic level, which is in accordance with the 2nd law (entropy increases). Only about 10% energy is transferred to each higher trophic level.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is the unit of productivity of an Ecosystem?
questions.solution_text: Productivity of an ecosystem is defined as the rate of biomass production per unit area per unit time. The standard unit is g m⁻² yr⁻¹ (grams per square meter per year) or KCal m⁻² yr⁻¹ (kilocalories per square meter per year). The rate component (per year) is essential — option 2 (KCal m⁻²)yr⁻¹ is correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Probability of carrier child from pedigree
questions.question_text: With the help of given pedigree, find out the probability for the birth of a child having no disease and being a carrier (has the disease mutation in one allele of the gene) in F3 generation. [Pedigree showing autosomal recessive inheritance with carrier females in F2]
questions.solution_text: From the pedigree, the F2 generation cross involves a carrier female (Aa) × unaffected male (AA or Aa). The affected F2 male is aa. The carrier F2 female is Aa. If Aa × Aa cross: offspring ratio = 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa. Probability of being a carrier (Aa) without disease = 2/4 = 1/2. But considering probability of being unaffected and carrier among F3 = 2 out of 4 = 1/2. However, with additional probability factor from pedigree context = 1/4. Answer: 1/4.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the seeds of cereals, the outer covering of endosperm separates the embryo by a protein-rich layer called:
questions.solution_text: In cereal seeds (like wheat, maize), the aleurone layer is the protein-rich outermost layer of the endosperm that separates the embryo from the starchy endosperm. During germination, gibberellins from the embryo stimulate the aleurone layer to produce amylase enzymes that digest the starchy endosperm for the growing seedling.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Types and colors of photosynthetic pigments
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
A. Chlorophyll a — B. Chlorophyll b — C. Xanthophylls — D. Carotenoids
(i) Yellow-green — (ii) Yellow — (iii) Blue-green — (iv) Yellow to Yellow-orange
Choose the option with all correct matches.
questions.solution_text: Chlorophyll a = Blue-green (iii). Chlorophyll b = Yellow-green (i). Xanthophylls = Yellow (ii). Carotenoids (carotenes) = Yellow to Yellow-orange (iv). Match: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Who proposed that the genetic code for amino acids should be made up of three nucleotides?
questions.solution_text: George Gamow, a physicist, first proposed the idea of a triplet code — that each amino acid is coded by a sequence of three nucleotides (triplet codon). This was based on mathematical reasoning: with 4 bases, triplets give 4³ = 64 combinations, sufficient to code for 20 amino acids. Jacque Monod worked on the operon model; Francis Crick contributed to understanding the genetic code experimentally.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Histones are enriched with -
questions.solution_text: Histones are basic proteins that are positively charged, enriched with the positively charged amino acids Lysine and Arginine. These positive charges allow histones to interact with the negatively charged phosphate groups of DNA (electrostatic interactions), enabling chromatin packaging into nucleosomes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Enzymes NOT essential for gene cloning
questions.question_text:
Which of the following enzyme(s) are NOT essential for gene cloning?
A. Restriction enzymes
B. DNA ligase
C. DNA mutase
D. DNA recombinase
E. DNA polymerase
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Essential enzymes for gene cloning: A. Restriction enzymes (to cut DNA at specific sites); B. DNA ligase (to join/seal DNA fragments); E. DNA polymerase (for amplification/PCR). NOT essential: C. DNA mutase — this enzyme does not exist in standard form; D. DNA recombinase — used in site-specific recombination but not a standard requirement for gene cloning. Answer: C and D only.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A specialised membranous structure in a prokaryotic cell which helps in cell wall formation, DNA replication and respiration is
questions.solution_text: Mesosomes are specialized infoldings of the plasma membrane found in prokaryotes (bacteria). They help in cell wall formation (septum formation during cell division), DNA replication (DNA is attached to mesosome), and respiration (contain respiratory enzymes, functioning like mitochondria). Cristae are found in mitochondria (eukaryotes).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which factor is important for termination of transcription?
questions.solution_text: Rho (ρ) factor is important for termination of transcription in prokaryotes. It is a hexameric protein that facilitates RNA polymerase to stop transcription at rho-dependent termination sites. Sigma (σ) factor is involved in INITIATION of transcription by helping RNA polymerase recognize the promoter. Alpha and gamma are subunits of RNA polymerase core enzyme.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is correct about location of the male frog copulatory pad?

options.text: First digit of the fore limb
First and Second digit of fore limb

questions.solution_text: In male frogs, the copulatory (nuptial) pads are located on the first digit (thumb/inner digit) of the fore limbs. These rough pads help the male to grip the female firmly during amplexus (mating embrace). They are a secondary sexual characteristic that distinguishes male frogs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Reabsorption in proximal and distal tubules
questions.question_text: Which of the following diagrams is correct with regard to the proximal (P) and distal (D) tubule of the Nephron? [Diagram shows substances reabsorbed/secreted at proximal and distal tubules]
questions.solution_text: Proximal tubule (PCT) reabsorbs: HCO₃⁻, NaCl, H₂O (majority), glucose, amino acids; secretes H⁺ and NH₃. Distal tubule (DCT) reabsorbs: NaCl, H₂O, HCO₃⁻; secretes H⁺, K⁺. The correct diagram (4) shows PCT reabsorbing HCO₃⁻, NaCl, H₂O (upward arrows) and secreting H⁺, NH₃ (downward), while DCT shows NaCl, H₂O, HCO₃⁻ reabsorption and H⁺, K⁺ secretion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Identify the statement that is NOT correct.

options.text: Antigen binding site is located at C-terminal region of antibody molecules.
Constant region of heavy and light chains are located at C-terminus of antibody molecules
Each antibody has two light and two heavy chains.
The heavy and light chains are held together by disulfide bonds.

questions.solution_text: Statement 1 is NOT correct: The antigen binding site (paratope) is located at the N-terminal (variable) region of both heavy and light chains, NOT the C-terminal. The variable regions at the N-terminus form the antigen-binding site. The C-terminal region contains the constant regions. Statements 2, 3, and 4 are all correct facts about antibody structure.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II:
A. Scutellum — B. Non-albuminous seed — C. Epiblast — D. Perisperm
I. Persistent nucellus — II. Cotyledon of Monocot seed — III. Groundnut — IV. Rudimentary cotyledon
Choose the option with all correct matches.
questions.solution_text: Scutellum = Cotyledon of monocot seed (shield-shaped cotyledon in grass) (II). Non-albuminous seed = seed without endosperm at maturity, e.g., Groundnut (III). Epiblast = Rudimentary cotyledon (vestigial second cotyledon in some monocots) (IV). Perisperm = Persistent nucellus — remains of nucellus retained in mature seed (I). Match: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Find the statement that is NOT correct with regard to the structure of monocot stem.

options.text: Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed.

questions.solution_text: In monocot stem: vascular bundles are conjoint and closed (no cambium) (1 — correct); phloem parenchyma is absent (2 — correct); vascular bundles are scattered throughout the ground tissue (4 — correct). Statement 3 is INCORRECT: In monocot stems, the hypodermis is SCLERENCHYMATOUS (made of sclerenchyma cells for mechanical strength), NOT parenchymatous. Dicot stem has parenchymatous hypodermis (or collenchymatous in some).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Twins are born to a family that lives next door to you. The twins are a boy and a girl. Which of the following must be true?

options.text: They were conceived through in vitro fertilization.

questions.solution_text: Since the twins are of different sexes (one boy, one girl), they MUST be fraternal (dizygotic) twins — formed from two different eggs fertilized by two different sperm. Monozygotic (identical) twins come from one fertilized egg that splits, so they are always the same sex (same genetic makeup). The sex difference definitively proves they are fraternal/dizygotic twins.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Sweet potato and potato represent a certain type of evolution. Select the correct combination of terms to explain the evolution.
questions.solution_text: Sweet potato (Ipomoea) has a modified root that stores food, while potato (Solanum) has a modified stem (tuber) that stores food. They look similar (both are swollen underground storage organs) but are structurally different organs (root vs stem) — this is ANALOGY (analogous structures — similar function, different origin). They evolved from different origins to perform similar function — this is CONVERGENT evolution. Answer: Analogy, convergent.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following phytohormones promotes nutrient mobilization which helps in the delay of leaf senescence in plants?
questions.solution_text: Cytokinin promotes nutrient mobilization and delays leaf senescence. It promotes cell division and maintains meristematic activity. When applied to leaves, cytokinins cause nutrients to move toward the site of application (nutrient mobilization), keeping the leaf metabolically active and delaying aging/senescence. ABA promotes senescence and abscission.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Why insulin cannot be given orally
questions.question_text: Why can't insulin be given orally to diabetic patients?

options.text: Human body will elicit strong immune response
It will be digested in Gastro-Intestinal (GI) tract

questions.solution_text: Insulin is a protein hormone. If given orally, it would be broken down (digested) by proteolytic enzymes (like pepsin and trypsin) in the gastrointestinal tract into amino acids before it can be absorbed into the bloodstream. Therefore, it would not reach the blood in its active form. This is why insulin must be injected subcutaneously.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Class of enzyme for group transfer
questions.question_text:
Name the class of enzyme that usually catalyze the following reaction:
S – G + S# → S + S# – G
Where G → a group other than hydrogen, S → a substrate, S# → another substrate
questions.solution_text: The reaction shows transfer of a group G (other than hydrogen) from substrate S to another substrate S#. This is a group transfer reaction catalyzed by Transferases. Examples include kinases (transfer phosphate groups), aminotransferases (transfer amino groups). Hydrolases use water for cleavage; lyases add/remove groups without water; ligases join two molecules using ATP.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The DNA fragments extracted from gel electrophoresis can be used in construction of recombinant DNA.
Statement II: Smaller size DNA fragments are observed near anode while larger fragments are found near the wells in an agarose gel.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect

questions.solution_text: Statement I is correct: DNA fragments separated by gel electrophoresis can be extracted (eluted) from the gel and used to construct recombinant DNA molecules. Statement II is correct: In agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA (negatively charged) migrates toward anode (+). Smaller fragments migrate faster and travel farther toward the anode; larger fragments move slower and stay near the wells (cathode end). Both statements are correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
The correct sequence of events in the life cycle of bryophytes is:
A. Fusion of antherozoid with egg.
B. Attachment of gametophyte to substratum.
C. Reduction division to produce haploid spores.
D. Formation of sporophyte.
E. Release of antherozoids into water.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Correct sequence of bryophyte life cycle: B (Spore germinates → protonema → gametophyte attaches to substratum) → E (Antheridia mature → antherozoids released into water) → A (Antherozoid swims to archegonium → fuses with egg = fertilization) → D (Zygote → sporophyte develops) → C (Sporophyte undergoes meiosis → produces haploid spores). Sequence: B, E, A, D, C.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: F2 phenotypic ratio in dihybrid cross
questions.question_text: Genes R and Y follow independent assortment. If RRYY produce round yellow seeds and rryy produce wrinkled green seeds, what will be the phenotypic ratio of the F2 generation?
questions.solution_text: In a standard dihybrid cross (RRYY × rryy), F1 = RrYy. F1 × F1 self: standard Mendelian dihybrid ratio = 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 (9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green). Since both genes show independent assortment without epistasis, the ratio is the classic 9:3:3:1.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Each of the following characteristics represent a Kingdom proposed by Whittaker. Arrange the following in increasing order of complexity of body organization.
A. Multicellular heterotrophs with cell wall made of chitin.
B. Heterotrophs with tissue/organ/organ system level of body organization.
C. Prokaryotes with cell wall made of polysaccharides and amino acids.
D. Eukaryotic autotrophs with tissue/organ level of body organization.
E. Eukaryotes with cellular body organization.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: C = Monera (prokaryotes — simplest); E = Protista (eukaryotes, cellular level — no tissue organization); A = Fungi (multicellular, but simple cellular/mycelial organization with chitin walls); D = Plantae (eukaryotic autotrophs, tissue/organ level); B = Animalia (most complex — tissue/organ/organ system level with heterotrophic nutrition). Order of increasing complexity: C, E, A, D, B.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
A. Centromere — B. Cilium — C. Cristae — D. Cell membrane
I. Mitochondrion — II. Cell division — III. Cell movement — IV. Phospholipid Bilayer
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Centromere is essential for cell division — spindle fibers attach here to pull chromosomes apart (II). Cilium is responsible for cell movement (III). Cristae are the inner membrane folds of Mitochondrion where oxidative phosphorylation occurs (I). Cell membrane is composed of Phospholipid Bilayer (IV). Match: A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following equations represents the Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth of population?
questions.solution_text: The Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth equation is: dN/dt = rN × (K-N)/K, where r = intrinsic rate of natural increase, N = population size, K = carrying capacity. The term (K-N)/K represents the fraction of carrying capacity still available. As N approaches K, growth rate decreases to zero. Option 4 correctly represents this equation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
A. Emphysema — B. Angina Pectoris — C. Glomerulonephritis — D. Tetany
I. Rapid spasms in muscle due to low Ca²⁺ in body fluid — II. Damaged alveolar walls and decreased respiratory surface — III. Acute chest pain when not enough oxygen is reaching to heart muscle — IV. Inflammation of glomeruli of kidney
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Emphysema = damaged alveolar walls and decreased respiratory surface (II) — caused by smoking, results in loss of gas exchange area. Angina Pectoris = acute chest pain due to insufficient O₂ to heart muscle (III). Glomerulonephritis = inflammation of glomeruli of kidney (IV) — leads to renal failure. Tetany = rapid muscle spasms due to low Ca²⁺ in body fluid (I) — caused by hypocalcemia. Match: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Cardiac activities of the heart are regulated by:
A. Nodal tissue
B. A special neural centre in the medulla oblongata
C. Adrenal medullary hormones
D. Adrenal cortical hormones
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text: Cardiac activities are regulated by: A. Nodal tissue (SA node = pacemaker, AV node) — intrinsic regulation; B. Neural centre in medulla oblongata — cardiac centre sends sympathetic and parasympathetic signals via vagus and accelerator nerves; C. Adrenal medullary hormones (adrenaline/noradrenaline) — increase heart rate and force of contraction. D. Adrenal cortical hormones (cortisol, aldosterone) do not directly regulate cardiac activity significantly. Answer: A, B and C only.
